overall.assessment: Prema tematskom prikazu, podcast je pretežno usmjeren na Krista, obraćenje i Božje milosrđe: molitveni dio povezuje pobožnost s Isusovim životom, mukom i euharistijom, a biblijsko razmatranje naglašava Pavlovo odricanje od pouzdanja u vlastite zasluge te radost zbog izgubljenoga koji je pronađen. To podupire kršćansku sliku osobe kao nekoga koga Bog traži i poziva na obnovu, a ne otpisuje; ipak, iz samog sadržajnog sažetka nije moguće procijeniti kako su te teme stvarno obrazložene ni kako se u praksi predstavljaju post, geopolitika i donacije. Najvažnija teološka nejasnoća jest formulacija o Isusovu „silasku nad pakao i čistilište”, koju treba precizirati kako se ne bi pomiješali različiti pojmovi; svjedočanstvo o bolesti i postu također zahtijeva oprez da se osobno iskustvo ne pretvori u opći zdravstveni ili duhovni recept. Zbog tih ograda cjelina djeluje uglavnom usklađeno s Evanđeljem, uz potrebu za jasnim katehetskim razgraničenjima i odgovornim društvenim govorom.
seeds_of_logos: Molitve i otajstva krunice usredotočeni su na Isusa, njegovo milosrđe, muku, uskrsnuće i euharistiju te uključuju marijansku pobožnost u kristološki okvir.
Razmatranje Fil 3 potiče poniznost pred milošću: Pavao ne temelji svoju vrijednost na podrijetlu, statusu ili vlastitim zaslugama, nego na Kristu i pozivu na trajno obraćenje.

Tumačenje izgubljene ovce promiče nadu, traženje onoga koji se udaljio i zajedničku radost zbog obraćenja; crkveno tumačenje te prispodobe upozorava da nitko ne smije biti proglašen beznadno izgubljenim.

Poziv da se raduje obraćenju drugoga može oblikovati kulturu susreta umjesto osuđivanja i samopravednosti, ako se vjernici doista prikazuju kao zajednica koja traži i prima, a ne kao zatvoreni krug „pravednih”.

Uključivanje bolesnih, molitve za umiruće i molitvenog zajedništva diljem Hrvatske može izražavati solidarnost i skrb za ranjive; kršćanska društvena odgovornost obuhvaća i služenje bolesnima, siromašnima i opterećenima.
concerns: Izraz „silazak nad pakao i čistilište” teološki je nedovoljno određen i može sugerirati da se Kristov silazak među mrtve i nauk o čistilištu poistovjećuju. Budući da je riječ samo o sažetku, nije moguće zaključiti da podcast doista zastupa takvo poistovjećenje; ipak, formulaciju bi trebalo jasno objasniti.

Poruka „ne pouzdati se u čovjeka” može biti poticaj da se konačna nada polaže u Boga, ali bez nijanse može zvučati kao opće nepovjerenje prema ljudima, zajednici ili stručnoj pomoći. Slično tome, osobno svjedočanstvo o narkolepsiji i postu ne bi trebalo tumačiti kao dokaz da post liječi bolest ili kao obvezujuću uputu za druge.

Domoljubna inicijativa, geopolitika, članstvo i donacije sami po sebi nisu suprotni kršćanskoj vjeri. Rizik bi nastao ako bi se katolička pobožnost stopila s nacionalističkim isključivanjem, političkom agendom ili nedovoljno transparentnim prikupljanjem sredstava; tematski prikaz ne daje dovoljno podataka da bi se utvrdilo događa li se to.

Jezik molitve oslobođenja i duhovne zaštite treba ostati usmjeren na Krista, povjerenje u Boga i obraćenje, a ne stvarati dojam da molitvene formule djeluju kao automatska zaštita ili zamjena za odgovorno djelovanje i potrebnu stručnu skrb.
overall.theological_context: Fil 3 podupire središnju poruku o prvenstvu Krista i odricanju od samodostatnog pouzdanja u vlastite prednosti, dok Lk 15 prikazuje Božju radosnu potragu za izgubljenim i poziva zajednicu da se raduje obraćenju. Lumen gentium 8, kako je citiran u crkvenom izvoru, povezuje poslanje Crkve sa služenjem Kristu u siromašnima i onima koji trpe; crkveno socijalno učenje zato traži da se navještaj i pobožnost očituju i u stvarnoj brizi za bližnje. Crkveni izvori također naglašavaju da oslobođenje od grijeha i obraćenje srca nisu zamjena za društvenu odgovornost, nego njezin temelj, pa društvene i domoljubne teme valja prosuđivati prema istini, ljubavi i dostojanstvu svake osobe.

overall.assessment_en: According to the thematic overview, the podcast is predominantly focused on Christ, conversion, and God's mercy: the prayer portion connects devotion with Jesus's life, passion, and the Eucharist, while the biblical reflection emphasizes Paul's renunciation of reliance on his own merits and the joy over the lost one who has been found. This supports the Christian view of the human person as someone whom God seeks and calls to renewal, rather than writes off; nonetheless, from the content summary alone it is not possible to evaluate how these topics are actually substantiated or how fasting, geopolitics, and donations are presented in practice. The most important theological ambiguity is the phrasing regarding Jesus's “descent over hell and purgatory,” which needs to be made precise so as not to confuse distinct concepts; the testimony regarding illness and fasting also requires caution so that a personal experience is not turned into a general medical or spiritual prescription. Because of these reservations, the whole appears mainly aligned with the Gospel, with the need for clear catechetical distinctions and responsible social speech.
overall.theological_context_en: Phil 3 supports the central message of the primacy of Christ and the renunciation of self-sufficient reliance on one's own advantages, while Lk 15 depicts God's joyful search for the lost and calls the community to rejoice over conversion. Lumen gentium 8, as cited in the church source, connects the Church's mission with serving Christ in the poor and those who suffer; Catholic social teaching therefore requires that proclamation and devotion also manifest in real care for one's neighbors. Church sources also emphasize that deliverance from sin and conversion of heart are not a substitute for social responsibility, but its foundation, so social and patriotic topics must be judged according to truth, love, and the dignity of every person.
seeds_of_logos_en: The prayers and mysteries of the rosary are focused on Jesus, his mercy, passion, resurrection, and the Eucharist, and incorporate Marian devotion into a Christological framework.
The reflection on Phil 3 encourages humility before grace: Paul does not base his worth on lineage, status, or his own merits, but on Christ and the call to continuous conversion.

The interpretation of the lost sheep promotes hope, seeking out the one who has strayed, and common joy over conversion; church interpretation of this parable warns that no one must be declared hopelessly lost.

The call to rejoice over another's conversion can shape a culture of encounter instead of condemnation and self-righteousness, if believers are truly presented as a community that seeks and receives, rather than as a closed circle of the “righteous.”

The inclusion of the sick, prayers for the dying, and prayer communion across Croatia can express solidarity and care for the vulnerable; Christian social responsibility also encompasses serving the sick, the poor, and the burdened.
concerns_en: The phrase “descent over hell and purgatory” is theologically insufficiently defined and may suggest that Christ's descent among the dead and the doctrine of purgatory are conflated. Since this is only a summary, it is not possible to conclude that the podcast actually advocates such a conflation; nonetheless, the formulation should be clearly explained.

The message “not to rely on man” can be an encouragement to place ultimate hope in God, but without nuance it can sound like general distrust toward people, community, or professional help. Similarly, the personal testimony about narcolepsy and fasting should not be interpreted as proof that fasting cures the illness or as a binding instruction for others.

The patriotic initiative, geopolitics, membership, and donations are not in themselves contrary to the Christian faith. The risk would arise if Catholic devotion were merged with nationalistic exclusion, a political agenda, or insufficiently transparent fundraising; the thematic overview does not provide enough data to determine whether this is occurring.

The language of the prayer of deliverance and spiritual protection should remain focused on Christ, trust in God, and conversion, rather than creating the impression that prayer formulas function as automatic protection or a substitute for responsible action and necessary professional care.

sections.subtitle: Radost neba zbog jednog obraćenog grešnika: molitveni susret otvara se zazivom zaštite
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj Vladimir Grebenar pozdravlja gledatelje, najavljuje evanđelje dana i započinje molitvu oslobođenja
sections.content:
Novu epizodu medija **Ora et Labora** voditelj **Vladimir Grebenar** otvara pozdravom „gledateljima i slušateljima“ i najavom evanđelja dana. Misao koja će obilježiti cijeli susret sažeta je u jednoj rečenici: **„Na nebu će biti radost zbog jednog obraćena grešnika.“** Odmah zatim, u ime Oca i Sina i Duha Svetoga, Grebenar započinje zajedničku molitvu, i to molitvom oslobođenja od zlih sila.

U toj molitvi voditelj u ime Isusovo „uzima vlast“ i veže sve zle sile i snage. Nabraja svaki prostor u kojem one mogu djelovati:

- u zraku,
- na zemlji,
- u vodi,
- u podzemlju,
- na onome svijetu,
- u prirodi,
- i u vatri.

Isusa ispovijeda kao **Gospodina nad svim svemirom** i daje mu slavu u ime svega stvorenja. Zatim veže „sve demonske sile koje su došle protiv nas i naših obitelji“ i sve koji mole stavlja pod zaštitu Kristove dragocjene krvi, prolivene na križu.

Molitva se potom obraća Mariji. Grebenar traži njezinu zaštitu i zagovor kod Presvetog Srca Isusova za sve obitelji, uz molbu: **„Zaogrni nas svojim plaštem ljubavi, da se prestraši neprijatelj.“** U pomoć zaziva i svetog Mihovila te anđele čuvare da brane molitelje i njihove obitelji „u borbi protiv svega zla što obilazi svijetom“. U ime Isusovo zapovijeda silama zla da istog časa odstupe od molitelja, njihovih domova i njihove zemlje. Uvodni dio završava zahvalom Isusu, „jer si vjeran Bog i osjećaš s nama“.

magisterium.assessment: Usmjerenost na Kristovu pobjedu nad zlom, molba za zaštitu njegovom krvlju te zagovor Marije i svetog Mihovila u skladu su s katoličkom molitvenom predajom. Ipak, govor o uzimanju vlasti, vezivanju svih zlih sila i zapovijedanju da odmah odu može zamagliti razliku između privatne molitve za zaštitu i službenog egzorcizma, koji se obavlja javno i s crkvenim autoritetom.
concerns: Formulacija koja kao da molitelju daje neposrednu vlast nad svim zlim silama može zvučati kao da je riječ o njegovoj vlastitoj moći, umjesto o molitvi koja se pouzdaje u Krista i traži Božje djelovanje.

Nabrajanje zraka, zemlje, vode, podzemlja, onoga svijeta, prirode i vatre nije samo po sebi naukovna pogreška, ali može ostaviti nejasan dojam da su sve te sfere posebno ili jednako pod demonskim utjecajem.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva moli za oslobođenje od Zloga i priznaje duhovnu borbu, ali službeni obred razlikuje molitvu vjernika od egzorcizma koji se vrši javno u ime i s autoritetom Crkve. Zato je prikladno privatne zazive oblikovati kao molbe Bogu za zaštitu, ne kao dojam da molitelj samostalno upravlja duhovnim silama; zazivanje Marije i anđela kao zagovornika i zaštitnika ima uporište u katoličkoj molitvenoj praksi.

Catholic Prayers for Protection Against Evil
citations.document_author: Catholic Bishops' Conference of England and Wales

magisterium.assessment_en: The focus on Christ's victory over evil, the petition for protection through his blood, and the intercession of Mary and Saint Michael are in accordance with Catholic prayer tradition. Nevertheless, talk of taking authority, binding all evil forces, and commanding them to leave immediately can blur the distinction between private prayer for protection and major exorcism, which is performed publicly and with church authority.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church prays for deliverance from the Evil One and acknowledges spiritual warfare, but the official ritual distinguishes the prayer of the faithful from exorcism, which is performed publicly in the name and with the authority of the Church. Therefore, it is appropriate to formulate private invocations as petitions to God for protection, not as an impression that the person praying independently commands spiritual forces; invoking Mary and the angels as intercessors and protectors is grounded in Catholic prayer practice.
concerns_en: The phrasing that appears to grant the person praying direct authority over all evil forces can sound as if it were a matter of their own power, instead of a prayer that relies on Christ and seeks God's action.

The enumeration of air, earth, water, the underworld, the other world, nature, and fire is not in itself a doctrinal error, but it can leave an unclear impression that all these spheres are specifically or equally under demonic influence.

sections.subtitle_en: Joy in heaven over one repentant sinner: prayer meeting opens with an invocation of protection
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host Vladimir Grebenar greets viewers, announces the gospel of the day, and begins the prayer of deliverance
sections.content_en:
The host **Vladimir Grebenar** opens the new episode of the media **Ora et Labora** with a greeting to the "viewers and listeners" and an announcement of the gospel of the day. The thought that will mark the entire meeting is summarized in one sentence: **"There will be joy in heaven over one repentant sinner."** Immediately after, in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, Grebenar begins the common prayer, with a prayer of deliverance from evil forces.

In that prayer, the host in the name of Jesus "takes authority" and binds all evil forces and powers. He enumerates every space in which they can operate:

- in the air,
- on the earth,
- in the water,
- in the underworld,
- in the other world,
- in nature,
- and in fire.

He confesses Jesus as **Lord over the whole universe** and gives him glory in the name of all creation. Then he binds "all demonic forces that have come against us and our families" and places all who pray under the protection of Christ's precious blood, shed on the cross.

The prayer then turns to Mary. Grebenar asks for her protection and intercession with the Sacred Heart of Jesus for all families, with the petition: **"Clothe us with your mantle of love, so that the enemy may be terrified."** He also calls upon Saint Michael and the guardian angels for help to defend the intercessors and their families "in the fight against all evil that roams the world." In the name of Jesus, he commands the forces of evil to depart immediately from the intercessors, their homes, and their land. The introductory part concludes with thanks to Jesus, "for you are a faithful God and you empathize with us."

sections.subtitle: Vojvoda vojske nebeske i nježni zaziv „Moj ljupki Isuse“
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar moli molitvu svetom Mihaelu arkanđelu
sections.content:
Na molitvu oslobođenja Vladimir Grebenar nadovezuje tradicionalnu **molitvu svetom Mihaelu arkanđelu**. Arkanđela moli da brani vjernike „u boju protiv pakosti i zasjeda đavolskih“ i da im bude zaklon. Mihaela oslovljava kao **„vojvodu vojske nebeske“** i ponizno moli da „Sotonu i druge duhove zlobne, koji svijetom obilaze na propast duša“, božanskom krepošću i jakošću strovali u pakao.

Nakon odlučnih riječi borbe slijedi molitva drukčijeg tona, **„Moj ljupki Isuse“**. U njoj se moli za potpuno jedinstvo s Kristom i među samim moliteljima. Molitva u nizu slika nabraja što se želi ujediniti:

- da noge „zajedno hode“,
- da ruke budu „skupljene u jedinstvu“,
- da srca „kucaju zajedno“,
- da duše budu „u skladu“, a misli „kao jedno“,
- da uši „zajedno slušaju tišinu“,
- da pogledi „duboko prodru jedan u drugi“.

Molitva završava molbom da usne zajedno mole „da zadobijemo milosrđe od vječnoga Oca“. Time se već na početku najavljuje središnja tema epizode, Božje milosrđe.

magisterium.assessment: Molitva svetom Mihaelu odgovara poznatoj katoličkoj molitvi koja se nalazi i u crkvenom obredniku, a molba za jedinstvo s Kristom i među moliteljima usmjerena je prema zajedničkoj molitvi i Božjem milosrđu. Izrazito pjesničke slike zajedništva nisu problematične dok ne znače brisanje osobnosti ili savjesti pojedinca.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkvena molitva svetom Mihaelu izričito ga zaziva da brani vjernike u duhovnoj borbi i moli Boga da Sotonu i zle duhove odbaci; takav je zaziv molba za Božju zaštitu, a ne pripisivanje božanske moći arkanđelu. Naglasak na zajedništvu može se razumjeti kao molitva da se različiti članovi okupe u Kristu i zajedno traže Očevo milosrđe, a ne kao zahtjev da svi moraju misliti ili osjećati na isti način.

Catholic Prayers for Protection Against Evil
citations.document_author: Catholic Bishops' Conference of England and Wales

magisterium.assessment_en: The prayer to Saint Michael corresponds to the well-known Catholic prayer that is also found in the church ritual book, and the petition for unity with Christ and among those praying is directed toward common prayer and God's mercy. Highly poetic imagery of communion is not problematic as long as it does not imply the erasure of an individual's personality or conscience.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church's prayer to Saint Michael explicitly invokes him to defend believers in spiritual warfare and begs God to cast down Satan and evil spirits; such an invocation is a petition for God's protection, not an attribution of divine power to the archangel. The emphasis on communion can be understood as a prayer that diverse members may be gathered in Christ and together seek the Father's mercy, rather than as a requirement that everyone must think or feel in the same way.

sections.subtitle_en: Commander of the heavenly host and the tender invocation "My sweet Jesus"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar prays the prayer to Saint Michael the Archangel
sections.content_en:
Following the prayer of deliverance, Vladimir Grebenar continues with the traditional **prayer to Saint Michael the Archangel**. He asks the archangel to defend the faithful "in battle against the wickedness and snares of the devil" and to be their safeguard. He addresses Michael as the **"commander of the heavenly host"** and humbly prays that he, by the divine power and strength, cast into hell "Satan and all evil spirits who roam through the world for the ruin of souls."

After the resolute words of warfare follows a prayer of a different tone, **"My sweet Jesus"**. In it, a prayer is made for complete unity with Christ and among the intercessors themselves. The prayer enumerates in a series of images what is desired to be united:

- that feet "walk together",
- that hands be "gathered in unity",
- that hearts "beat together",
- that souls be "in harmony", and thoughts "as one",
- that ears "together listen to the silence",
- that glances "penetrate deeply into one another".

The prayer concludes with a petition that lips pray together "that we may obtain mercy from the eternal Father". Thereby, right at the beginning, the central theme of the episode, God's mercy, is announced.

sections.subtitle: Predanje cijelog bića: posveta Bezgrešnom Srcu Marijinu i Presvetom Srcu Isusovu
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj moli molitvu posvete Bezgrešnom Srcu Marijinu
sections.content:
Sljedeći dio molitvenog susreta posvećen je **posveti**. Vladimir Grebenar Presvetu Djevicu Mariju oslovljava kao „majku i kraljicu“ te njezinu bezgrešnom srcu posvećuje i predaje „čitavo svoje biće, svoje misli, riječi i djela“. Molitva ide i dalje: moli Mariju da raspolaže molitateljem i svime što mu pripada, „sada i u vječnosti“. Sve to čini na hvalu i slavu Presvetoga Trojstva, za posvećenje Crkve i spasenje svega svijeta.

U posveti posebno mjesto ima **krsno posvećenje**. Voditelj moli Mariju da mu pomogne živjeti dostojno tog posvećenja, kako bi neopozivo pripadao svome Otkupitelju. Moli i da poput nje sluša poticaje Duha Svetoga, uz zaključni zaziv: **„Neka se u meni i u svemu vrši volja Božja.“**

Zatim slijedi molitva **Presvetom Srcu Isusovu**, koje se naziva „izvorom svakoga dobra“. Molitelj mu se klanja, vjeruje u njega, ufa se u njega, ljubi ga i kaje se za svoje grijehe. Isusu poklanja svoje „siromašno srce“ i moli da ga učini poniznim, strpljivim i čistim te da u svemu odgovara njegovim željama. Uz molbu „da ja živim u tebi i ti u meni“, nabraja se i niz konkretnih potreba:

- zaštita u opasnostima,
- utjeha u nevoljama i žalostima,
- zdravlje tijela,
- blagoslov za sav rad,
- milost svete smrti.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je u skladu s katoličkom pobožnošću: predanje Mariji usmjereno je na Presveto Trojstvo, vjernost krsnom posvećenju i pripadnost Kristu, a molitva Presvetom Srcu Isusovu izražava vjeru, pouzdanje, ljubav, kajanje i molbu za milosti. Nema očitog naukovnog proturječja; traženje zdravlja i pomoći u potrebama valja razumjeti kao prošnju, a ne kao jamstvo da će svaka molba biti uslišena na željeni način.
concerns: Izraz „posveta Mariji” treba razumjeti analogno, kao povjeravanje njezinu zagovoru i majčinskoj brizi, a ne kao božansko štovanje ili posvetu neovisnu o Bogu; crkveni vodič naglašava da se takvo predanje usmjerava Ocu po Kristu u Duhu Svetom.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkveni vodič prihvaća povjeravanje Mariji kao način vjernijeg življenja krsnih obveza, uz napomenu da se ono bitno razlikuje od liturgijske posvete Bogu. Pobožnost Bezgrešnom Srcu Marijinu vodi prema Srcu njezina Sina, dok je pobožnost Presvetom Srcu Isusovu usmjerena Kristu i njegovoj otkupiteljskoj ljubavi.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is in accordance with Catholic devotion: entrustment to Mary is directed toward the Most Holy Trinity, fidelity to baptismal consecration, and belonging to Christ, while the prayer to the Most Sacred Heart of Jesus expresses faith, trust, love, repentance, and a petition for graces. There is no apparent doctrinal contradiction; seeking health and help in necessities should be understood as a petition, not as a guarantee that every request will be granted in the desired manner.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The church guide accepts entrustment to Mary as a way of living baptismal commitments more faithfully, with the note that it differs essentially from liturgical consecration to God. Devotion to the Immaculate Heart of Mary leads toward the Heart of her Son, while devotion to the Most Sacred Heart of Jesus is directed to Christ and his redemptive love.
concerns_en: The term “consecration to Mary” should be understood analogously, as an entrustment to her intercession and maternal care, and not as divine worship or a consecration independent of God; the church guide emphasizes that such surrender is directed to the Father through Christ in the Holy Spirit.

sections.subtitle_en: Surrender of the whole being: consecration to the Immaculate Heart of Mary and the Sacred Heart of Jesus
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host prays the prayer of consecration to the Immaculate Heart of Mary
sections.content_en:
The next part of the prayer meeting is dedicated to **consecration**. Vladimir Grebenar addresses the Blessed Virgin Mary as "mother and queen" and consecrates and surrenders to her immaculate heart "his entire being, his thoughts, words, and deeds." The prayer goes further: it asks Mary to dispose of the person praying and everything that belongs to him, "now and in eternity." All this is done for the praise and glory of the Most Holy Trinity, for the sanctification of the Church, and the salvation of the whole world.

In the consecration, a special place is held by the **baptismal consecration**. The host asks Mary to help him live worthily of that consecration, so that he may belong irrevocably to his Redeemer. He also prays to listen, like her, to the promptings of the Holy Spirit, with the concluding invocation: **"May the will of God be done in me and in everything."**

Then follows the prayer to the **Sacred Heart of Jesus**, which is called the "fount of every good." The person praying adores it, believes in it, hopes in it, loves it, and repents of his sins. He presents Jesus with his "poor heart" and prays that he make it humble, patient, and pure, and that it conform in everything to his desires. Along with the petition "that I may live in you and you in me," a series of concrete needs is also enumerated:

- protection in dangers,
- comfort in afflictions and sorrows,
- health of the body,
- blessing for all work,
- the grace of a holy death.

sections.subtitle: Temelj kršćanske molitve: Oče naš, Zdravo Marijo i Vjerovanje
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar izgovara Apostolsko vjerovanje
sections.content:
Prije krunice Božanskom milosrđu Vladimir Grebenar moli tri temeljne molitve kršćanske tradicije. Prva je **Oče naš**, Gospodnja molitva koja moli da se sveti Božje ime, da dođe njegovo kraljevstvo i da se vrši njegova volja „kako na nebu tako i na zemlji“. U njoj se traži i svagdanji kruh, oproštenje dugova i izbavljenje od zla.

Slijedi **Zdravo Marijo**, pozdrav Djevici koja je „milosti puna“ i molba Majci Božjoj da moli za grešnike „sada i na času smrti naše“.

Treća je **Vjerovanje**, ispovijest vjere u Boga Oca svemogućega, stvoritelja neba i zemlje, i u Isusa Krista. Vjerovanje sažima Kristov put: začet je po Duhu Svetom, rođen od Marije Djevice, mučen pod Poncijem Pilatom, raspet, umro i pokopan, sašao nad pakao, treći dan uskrsnuo i uzašao na nebesa, odakle će doći suditi žive i mrtve. Ispovijest završava vjerom u Duha Svetoga, svetu Crkvu katoličku, općinstvo svetih, oproštenje grijeha, uskrsnuće tijela i život vječni.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak vjerno prenosi sadržaj i katoličko značenje Očenaša, Zdravo Marijo i Apostolskog vjerovanja te je u skladu sa Svetim pismom i katoličkom molitvenom predajom. Nema uočljivih teoloških problema u opisu tih molitava.
magisterium.enrichment: Očenaš je, prema Katekizmu i njegovu Kompendiju, sažetak cijelog Evanđelja i uzor kršćanske molitve. Zdravo Marijo uključuje biblijski pozdrav Mariji i molbu za njezin zagovor, a Vjerovanje sažima temeljne istine kršćanske vjere, uključujući Kristovo utjelovljenje, smrt i uskrsnuće te nadu u uskrsnuće tijela i život vječni.

citations.document_title: Compendium of the Catechism of the Catholic Church

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage faithfully conveys the content and Catholic meaning of the Our Father, Hail Mary, and Apostles' Creed, and is in accordance with Sacred Scripture and Catholic prayer tradition. There are no noticeable theological issues in the description of these prayers.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Our Father is, according to the Catechism and its Compendium, the summary of the whole Gospel and the model of Christian prayer. The Hail Mary includes the biblical greeting to Mary and a petition for her intercession, and the Creed summarizes the fundamental truths of the Christian faith, including Christ's incarnation, death, and resurrection, as well as the hope of the resurrection of the body and life everlasting.

sections.subtitle_en: The foundation of Christian prayer: Our Father, Hail Mary, and the Creed
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar recites the Apostles' Creed
sections.content_en:
Before the chaplet of Divine Mercy, Vladimir Grebenar prays three fundamental prayers of the Christian tradition. The first is the **Our Father**, the Lord's Prayer which prays that God's name be hallowed, that his kingdom come, and that his will be done "on earth as it is in heaven." In it, daily bread, forgiveness of debts, and deliverance from evil are also asked for.

Next is the **Hail Mary**, a greeting to the Virgin who is "full of grace" and a petition to the Mother of God to pray for sinners "now and at the hour of our death."

The third is the **Creed**, a profession of faith in God the Father almighty, creator of heaven and earth, and in Jesus Christ. The Creed summarizes Christ's journey: he was conceived by the Holy Spirit, born of the Virgin Mary, suffered under Pontius Pilate, was crucified, died, and was buried, descended into hell, on the third day rose again, and ascended into heaven, from where he will come to judge the living and the dead. The profession concludes with faith in the Holy Spirit, the holy Catholic Church, the communion of saints, the forgiveness of sins, the resurrection of the body, and life everlasting.

sections.subtitle: „Po njegovoj pregorkoj muci“: krunica Božanskom milosrđu za cijeli svijet
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj započinje krunicu Božanskom milosrđu riječima „Vječni Oče, prikazujemo ti tijelo i krv…“
sections.content:
Središnji dio prvog molitvenog bloka, u skladu s naslovom epizode, čini **krunica Božanskom milosrđu**. Vladimir Grebenar svaku od pet desetica otvara istom prikaznom molitvom: **„Vječni Oče, prikazujemo ti tijelo i krv, dušu i božanstvo preljubljenoga Sina tvojega, Gospodina našega Isusa Krista, kao zadovoljštinu za grijehe naše i cijeloga svijeta.“**

Nakon toga deset puta ponavlja zaziv koji nosi cijelu krunicu: **„Po njegovoj pregorkoj muci, budi milosrdan nama i cijelome svijetu.“**

U središtu ove molitve je Kristova muka, prikazana Ocu kao zadovoljština. Molitva ne ostaje ograničena na one koji mole, nego svaki zaziv obuhvaća „cijeli svijet“. Ritmično i mirno ponavljanje, desetica za deseticom, traje nekoliko minuta. Tako se gledatelji i slušatelji uvode u dugu, meditativnu molitvu, otvorenu prema milosrđu za sve ljude.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je usklađen s katoličkim naukom: Krunica Božanskom milosrđu usredotočuje se na jedinstvenu Kristovu žrtvu i moli milosrđe za sve ljude, što je u skladu s katoličkim razumijevanjem Božje spasenjske volje. Govor o Kristovoj muci kao zadovoljštini pravovjeran je ako se razumije kao oslanjanje na Kristovo potpuno otkupiteljsko djelo, a ne kao ponavljanje ili nadopunjavanje njegove žrtve.
magisterium.enrichment: U ovoj molitvi vjernici ne prikazuju Ocu novu žrtvu, nego se molitveno sjedinjuju s Kristovom žrtvom i mole da njezini plodovi zahvate njih i cijeli svijet; takvo značenje izričito se povezuje s molitvom Krunice Božanskom milosrđu. Krist je svojom mukom zadovoljio za grijehe ljudskoga roda, a njegovo djelo objavljuje istodobno Božju pravdu i milosrđe.

citations.document_title: Diary of Saint Maria Faustina Kowalska: Divine Mercy in My Soul

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is aligned with Catholic teaching: the Chaplet of the Divine Mercy focuses on Christ's unique sacrifice and implores mercy for all people, which is in accordance with the Catholic understanding of God's universal salvific will. Speaking of Christ's passion as satisfaction is orthodox if it is understood as relying on Christ's complete redemptive work, and not as repeating or supplementing his sacrifice.
magisterium.enrichment_en: In this prayer, the faithful do not offer the Father a new sacrifice, but unite themselves in prayer with Christ's sacrifice and pray that its fruits may reach them and the whole world; such meaning is explicitly connected with the recitation of the Chaplet of the Divine Mercy. By his passion, Christ made satisfaction for the sins of the human race, and his work reveals both God's justice and mercy at the same time.

sections.subtitle_en: "For the sake of his sorrowful passion": chaplet of Divine Mercy for the whole world
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host begins the chaplet of Divine Mercy with the words "Eternal Father, I offer you the body and blood…"
sections.content_en:
The central part of the first prayer block, in accordance with the episode title, is the **chaplet of Divine Mercy**. Vladimir Grebenar opens each of the five decades with the same offering prayer: **"Eternal Father, we offer you the body and blood, soul and divinity of your dearly beloved Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, in atonement for our sins and those of the whole world."**

After that, he repeats ten times the invocation that carries the entire chaplet: **"For the sake of his sorrowful passion, have mercy on us and on the whole world."**

At the center of this prayer is Christ's passion, offered to the Father as atonement. The prayer does not remain limited to those who pray, but each invocation encompasses "the whole world." The rhythmic and calm repetition, decade after decade, lasts for several minutes. In this way, viewers and listeners are introduced into a long, meditative prayer, open toward mercy for all people.

sections.subtitle: Sveti Bože, krv i voda iz Srca Isusova i trostruko „Isuse, uzdam se u tebe“
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar moli završne zazive krunice Božanskom milosrđu
sections.content:
Krunica Božanskom milosrđu završava trostrukim zazivom: **„Sveti Bože, sveti jaki Bože, sveti besmrtni Bože, smiluj se nama i cijelomu svijetu.“** Vladimir Grebenar ga izgovara tri puta, sabrano i polako.

Zatim slijedi zaziv koji milosrđe povezuje s ranjenim Kristovim Srcem: **„O krvi i vodo, što potekoste iz Srca Isusova kao izvor milosrđa za nas, uzdam se u tebe.“** Uz njega dolazi i kratka molba Mariji, kojoj se obraća kao **„majci milosrđa“**: „Moli za nas.“

Vrhunac ovog dijela je tri puta ponovljeno **„Isuse, uzdam se u tebe“**, zaziv pouzdanja koji je jezgra pobožnosti Božanskom milosrđu. Za njim slijedi još jedna molba za smilovanje „nama i cijelomu svijetu“.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je u skladu s katoličkom vjerom i biblijskom slikom probodenog Kristova boka: Ivanovo evanđelje svjedoči da su iz njega potekle krv i voda, a Crkva ih tumači kao znamenja povezana s Kristovom žrtvom, krštenjem, darom Duha i životom Crkve. Zaziv Mariji da moli za nas izražava njezin zagovor, a „Isuse, uzdam se u tebe“ usmjerava pouzdanje prema Kristu, izvoru milosrđa.
magisterium.enrichment: Ivan 19,34 daje biblijsku podlogu zazivu o krvi i vodi iz Kristova boka; papa Ivan Pavao II. povezuje krv s Kristovom žrtvom i euharistijskim darom, a vodu s krštenjem i darom Duha Svetoga. Marijina molba „Moli za nas“ ne stavlja je na mjesto Krista, nego traži njezin zagovor u povezanosti s Kristovim otkupiteljskim djelom.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is in accordance with the Catholic faith and the biblical imagery of Christ's pierced side: John's Gospel testifies that blood and water flowed from it, and the Church interprets them as signs connected with Christ's sacrifice, baptism, the gift of the Spirit, and the life of the Church. The invocation to Mary to pray for us expresses her intercession, and “Jesus, I trust in you” directs trust toward Christ, the source of mercy.
magisterium.enrichment_en: John 19:34 provides the biblical foundation for the invocation concerning the blood and water from Christ's side; Pope John Paul II connects the blood with Christ's sacrifice and the Eucharistic gift, and the water with baptism and the gift of the Holy Spirit. Mary's petition “Pray for us” does not place her in the position of Christ, but asks for her intercession in connection with Christ's redemptive work.

sections.subtitle_en: Holy God, blood and water from the Heart of Jesus, and the triple "Jesus, I trust in you"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar prays the concluding invocations of the chaplet of Divine Mercy
sections.content_en:
The chaplet of Divine Mercy concludes with a triple invocation: **"Holy God, Holy Mighty One, Holy Immortal One, have mercy on us and on the whole world."** Vladimir Grebenar recites it three times, collectedly and slowly.

Then follows an invocation connecting mercy with the wounded Heart of Christ: **"O blood and water, which gushed forth from the Heart of Jesus as a fount of mercy for us, I trust in you."** Alongside it comes also a brief petition to Mary, who is addressed as **"mother of mercy"**: "Pray for us."

The peak of this part is the three times repeated **"Jesus, I trust in you"**, an invocation of trust that is the core of devotion to Divine Mercy. Following it is another petition for mercy "on us and on the whole world."

sections.subtitle: Litanije Božjem milosrđu: od stvaranja svijeta do utjehe umirućih
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj moli litanije, ponavljajući odgovor „uzdam se u tebe“
sections.content:
Nakon krunice Vladimir Grebenar moli **Litanije Božjem milosrđu**. Počinju uobičajenim litanijskim zazivima „Gospodine, smiluj se“ i „Kriste, smiluj se“, nakon kojih se zaziva svaka božanska osoba: Oče nebeski, Sine, Otkupitelju svijeta, Duše Sveti i Sveto Trojstvo, jedan Bože.

Slijedi dugi niz zaziva u kojima se Božje milosrđe slavi pod mnogim vidovima. Na svaki se odgovara: **„uzdam se u tebe“**. Milosrđe Božje u litanijama je, među ostalim:

- „neshvatljiva tajna Presvetoga Trojstva“ i „izraz njegove najveće moći“,
- ono što se objavilo u stvaranju nebeskih duhova i što je ljude „iz ništavila pozvalo u život“,
- ono koje obuhvaća čitav svijet i daruje besmrtan život,
- ono koje štiti od zasluženih kazna i oslobađa od bijede grijeha,
- ono koje se izlijeva iz rana Kristovih i izvire iz Presvetog Srca,
- ono koje je ljudima dalo Presvetu Djevicu za majku milosrđa,
- ono vidljivo u ustanovljenju Crkve koja obuhvaća cijeli svijet i u dijeljenju svetih sakramenata,
- neograničeno u sakramentu krštenja i pokore te neizmjerno u sakramentu oltara i svećeništva,
- ono koje je ljude pozvalo k svetoj vjeri,
- prisutno u obraćenju grešnika, ono koje posvećuje pravednike i usavršava svete,
- vrelo bolesnicima i patnicima, utjeha onih „skršena srca“ i ufanje onih koji očajavaju,
- „mir umirućih“, zaštita od paklenoga ognja i olakšanje patnje dušama u čistilištu,
- slast i neizmjerna radost svih svetih te „neiscrpiv izvor čudesa“.

Osobito se ističe zaziv milosrđu „u obraćenju grešnika“, koji izravno odjekuje evanđeljem dana o radosti neba zbog jednog obraćenog grešnika.

magisterium.assessment: Opisane litanije u skladu su s katoličkom vjerom: usmjeravaju pouzdanje Bogu, slave njegovo milosrđe i povezuju ga s Kristovim otkupiteljskim djelom, životom Crkve i sakramentima. Naglasak na obraćenju grešnika odgovara evanđeoskoj radosti zbog obraćenja (Lk 15,7.10), a molitva za duše u čistilištu u skladu je s katoličkom praksom zagovora za pokojne (2 Mak 12,44–46).
magisterium.enrichment: Milosrđe u katoličkom razumijevanju nije samo osjećaj Božje blagosti, nego dar oproštenja i spasenja koji se prima u životu Crkve; papa Franjo izrijekom povezuje crkvenu molitvu za milosrđe sa sakramentalnim životom, osobito pomirenjem i euharistijom. Zaziv „uzdam se u tebe” izražava pouzdanje u Boga, ali ne znači da su obraćenje i spasenje nevažni niti da je čovjek automatski zaštićen od posljedica grijeha.
magisterium.assessment_en: The described litanies are in accordance with the Catholic faith: they direct trust toward God, praise his mercy, and connect it with Christ's redemptive work, the life of the Church, and the sacraments. The emphasis on the conversion of sinners corresponds to evangelical joy over conversion (Lk 15:7, 10), and prayer for the souls in purgatory is in accordance with the Catholic practice of intercession for the deceased (2 Macc 12:44–46).
magisterium.enrichment_en: Mercy in the Catholic understanding is not merely a feeling of God's gentleness, but the gift of forgiveness and salvation received in the life of the Church; Pope Francis explicitly connects the Church's prayer for mercy with sacramental life, especially reconciliation and the Eucharist. The invocation “I trust in you” expresses trust in God, but it does not mean that conversion and salvation are unimportant or that man is automatically protected from the consequences of sin.

sections.subtitle_en: Litany of the Divine Mercy: from the creation of the world to the consolation of the dying
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host prays the litany, repeating the response "I trust in you"
sections.content_en:
After the chaplet, Vladimir Grebenar prays the **Litany of the Divine Mercy**. It begins with the usual litany invocations "Lord, have mercy" and "Christ, have mercy", after which each divine person is invoked: Heavenly Father, Son, Redeemer of the world, Holy Spirit, and Holy Trinity, one God.

There follows a long series of invocations in which God's mercy is praised under many aspects. To each, the response is: **"I trust in you"**. Divine mercy in the litany is, among other things:

- "the unfathomable mystery of the Most Holy Trinity" and "the expression of his greatest power",
- that which was revealed in the creation of heavenly spirits and which "called humans from nothingness into life",
- that which encompasses the entire world and bestows immortal life,
- that which shields from deserved punishments and liberates from the misery of sin,
- that which pours out from the wounds of Christ and flows from the Sacred Heart,
- that which gave humans the Blessed Virgin for the mother of mercy,
- that which is visible in the establishment of the Church that encompasses the entire world and in the administration of the holy sacraments,
- unlimited in the sacrament of baptism and penance and immense in the sacrament of the altar and priesthood,
- that which called humans to the holy faith,
- present in the conversion of sinners, that which sanctifies the righteous and perfects the holy,
- a spring for the sick and suffering, the consolation of those "of a broken heart" and the hope of those who despair,
- the "peace of the dying", protection from the fire of hell, and relief of suffering for the souls in purgatory,
- the delight and immense joy of all saints and an "inexhaustible source of miracles".

Particularly emphasized is the invocation to mercy "in the conversion of sinners", which directly echoes the gospel of the day about the joy of heaven over one repentant sinner.

sections.subtitle: Da u teškim trenucima ne očajavamo: završna molitva vječnom Bogu
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar izgovara završnu molitvu litanija vječnom Bogu
sections.content:
Litanije završavaju psalmodijskim retkom: **„Bog je milosrdan i pun samilosti, spor na srđbu i pun dobrote. Zato ću dovijeka klicati milosrđu Božjemu.“**

Vladimir Grebenar zatim moli završnu molitvu vječnom Bogu, „čije je milosrđe neistraživo i čije je blago smilovanja neiscrpivo“. Moli da Bog milosno pogleda na vjernike i umnoži u njima svoje milosrđe. Svrha te molbe izrečena je jasno: **„da u teškim trenucima ne očajavamo i ne budemo obeshrabreni“**, nego da se s velikim pouzdanjem predaju Božjoj svetoj volji, „koja je sama ljubav i smilovanje“.

Molitva se zaključuje po Gospodinu Isusu Kristu, kojeg se naziva **„kraljem milosrđa“** i koji s Ocem i Duhom Svetim iskazuje milosrđe u sve vijeke vjekova. Time završava blok posvećen Božanskom milosrđu.

magisterium.assessment: Završna molitva pouzdanja i ustrajnosti u teškoćama u skladu je s kršćanskom nadom: vjernik se oslanja na Božje milosrđe, a ne na uvjerenje da će izbjeći svaku patnju. Nazivi Isusa „kraljem milosrđa” i molitva Trojedinom Bogu u skladu su s katoličkom vjerom u Kristovo kraljevanje i djelovanje Presvetoga Trojstva.
magisterium.enrichment: Molitva da se u kušnjama ne očajava ne poriče ozbiljnost boli, nego potiče nadu i vjernost Bogu. Izraz da je Božja volja ljubav i smilovanje valja razumjeti kao ispovijest pouzdanja u Božju dobrotu, a ne kao tvrdnju da je svako bolno događanje samo po sebi dobro ili da se pred zlom ne treba zauzimati; kršćanska nada uči povjeravati Bogu i djelovati za dobro.

magisterium.assessment_en: The concluding prayer of trust and perseverance in difficulties is in accordance with Christian hope: the believer relies on God's mercy, rather than on the conviction that every suffering will be avoided. The titles of Jesus as “king of mercy” and the prayer to the Triune God are in accordance with Catholic faith in Christ's kingship and the activity of the Most Holy Trinity.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The prayer not to despair in trials does not deny the seriousness of pain, but fosters hope and fidelity to God. The expression that God's will is love and mercy should be understood as a confession of trust in God's goodness, and not as an assertion that every painful occurrence is good in itself or that one should not take action against evil; Christian hope teaches entrusting to God and acting for good.

sections.subtitle_en: That in difficult moments we may not despair: concluding prayer to the eternal God
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar recites the concluding prayer of the litany to the eternal God
sections.content_en:
The litany concludes with a psalmodic verse: **"God is merciful and full of compassion, slow to anger and abounding in kindness. Therefore I will praise the mercy of God forever."**

Vladimir Grebenar then prays the concluding prayer to the eternal God, "whose mercy is fathomless and whose treasury of compassion is inexhaustible." He prays that God look mercifully upon the faithful and increase his mercy in them. The purpose of this petition is stated clearly: **"that in difficult moments we may not despair and not be discouraged"**, but that with great confidence they surrender to God's holy will, "which is love and mercy itself."

The prayer is concluded through the Lord Jesus Christ, who is called the **"king of mercy"** and who with the Father and the Holy Spirit shows mercy for ages of ages. With this, the block dedicated to Divine Mercy concludes.

sections.subtitle: Otajstva svjetla: od Jordana do svadbe u Kani
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj najavljuje prvo otajstvo svjetla, Isusovo krštenje na rijeci Jordanu
sections.content:
Drugi veliki dio molitvenog susreta je **krunica otajstava svjetla**. Vladimir Grebenar najavljuje **prvo otajstvo**: Isus, koji je **na rijeci Jordanu kršten bio**. Svaka desetica ima isti, ustaljeni red:

- jedan **Oče naš**,
- deset **Zdravo Marijo**,
- **Slava Ocu**,
- molitva **„O moj Isuse“**.

U molitvi „O moj Isuse“ moli se za oproštenje grijeha, očuvanje od paklenoga ognja i da Isus u raj dovede sve duše, „a osobito one kojima je najpotrebnije tvoje milosrđe“. Ona tako i u krunici zadržava temu milosrđa koja prožima cijelu epizodu.

U **drugom otajstvu** razmatra se Isus, koji je **na svadbi u Kani objavio svoju slavu**. Ponovno slijede Oče naš, deset Zdravo Marija, Slava Ocu i zaziv „O moj Isuse“. Mirni i ujednačeni ritam ponavljanja omogućuje onima koji mole uz prijenos da se sabrano udube u svako otajstvo.

magisterium.assessment: Prvo i drugo otajstvo svjetla ispravno su navedeni: Isusovo krštenje na Jordanu i njegovo očitovanje na svadbi u Kani dio su crkveno prihvaćenog niza otajstava svjetla. Opis molitve O moj Isuse kao prošnje za milosrđe ne iznosi nauk koji bi bio u sukobu s katoličkom vjerom.
magisterium.enrichment: Krštenje na Jordanu objavljuje Isusa kao ljubljenoga Sina, a silazak Duha Svetoga očituje njegovo poslanje. U Kani Isusov prvi znak potiče učenike na vjeru, a Marijina uloga pokazuje kako ih ona usmjerava prema Kristu; zato ova otajstva osvjetljuju Isusov identitet i početak njegova javnog djelovanja.

magisterium.assessment_en: The first and second luminous mysteries are correctly stated: Jesus's baptism in the Jordan and his manifestation at the wedding in Cana are part of the church-accepted set of luminous mysteries. Describing the prayer “O My Jesus” as a petition for mercy does not set forth teaching that would be in conflict with the Catholic faith.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The baptism in the Jordan reveals Jesus as the beloved Son, and the descent of the Holy Spirit manifests his mission. At Cana, Jesus's first sign prompts the disciples to faith, and Mary's role shows how she directs them toward Christ; therefore, these mysteries illuminate Jesus's identity and the beginning of his public ministry.

sections.subtitle_en: Luminous Mysteries: from the Jordan to the wedding at Cana
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host announces the first luminous mystery, Jesus' baptism in the Jordan River
sections.content_en:
The second major part of the prayer meeting is the **Rosary of the Luminous Mysteries**. Vladimir Grebenar announces the **first mystery**: Jesus, who **was baptized in the Jordan River**. Each decade follows the same, established order:

- one **Our Father**,
- ten **Hail Marys**,
- **Glory Be to the Father**,
- the prayer **"O my Jesus"**.

In the prayer "O my Jesus", prayer is made for the forgiveness of sins, preservation from the fire of hell, and that Jesus lead all souls to heaven, "especially those who are in most need of your mercy". It thus also in the Rosary retains the theme of mercy that permeates the entire episode.

In the **second mystery**, contemplation is made on Jesus, who **at the wedding at Cana manifested his glory**. Again follow the Our Father, ten Hail Marys, the Glory Be, and the invocation "O my Jesus". The calm and steady rhythm of repetition enables those praying along with the broadcast to immerse themselves in each mystery with recollection.

sections.subtitle: „Obratite se, kraljevstvo Božje je blizu“ i svjetlo s gore Tabor
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar najavljuje treće otajstvo, navještaj kraljevstva Božjeg i poziv na obraćenje
sections.content:
**Treće otajstvo svjetla**, kako ga najavljuje Vladimir Grebenar, posvećeno je Isusu koji je navijestio: **„Obratite se, kraljevstvo Božje je blizu.“** Poziv na obraćenje u ovom otajstvu tematski se izravno nadovezuje na evanđelje dana kojim je epizoda otvorena, onim o radosti neba zbog jednog obraćenog grešnika. Krunica tako nastavlja nit koja povezuje sve dijelove molitve.

Zatim slijedi **četvrto otajstvo**: Isus, koji se **na gori Taboru preobrazio**. U oba otajstva voditelj se drži ustaljenog reda. Moli Oče naš, deset Zdravo Marija i Slava Ocu, a svaku deseticu zaključuje molbom „O moj Isuse, oprosti nam naše grijehe“, uz molitvu za duše kojima je Božje milosrđe najpotrebnije.

magisterium.assessment: Treće i četvrto otajstvo sadržajno odgovaraju otajstvima svjetla: Isusovo naviještanje Božjega kraljevstva uz poziv na obraćenje te njegovo preobraženje, koje se prema predaji zbilo na Taboru. Navod o kraljevstvu i obraćenju prikladno sažima Mk 1,15, ali ako je zamišljen kao doslovan biblijski citat, izostavlja poziv da se vjeruje evanđelju.
concerns: Navod „Obratite se, kraljevstvo Božje je blizu“ nije potpun doslovni navod Mk 1,15: u izvoru se uz obraćenje navodi i poziv na vjeru u evanđelje. To je manja nepreciznost citiranja, a ne bitno doktrinarno odstupanje.
magisterium.enrichment: Isusovo naviještanje kraljevstva povezuje obraćenje s njegovim djelovanjem milosrđa i oproštenja; obraćenje je stoga odgovor na Božji dolazak, a ne samo općenita promjena ponašanja. Preobraženje objavljuje Kristovu slavu i glas Oca poziva učenike da ga slušaju, pripremajući ih za put prema muci i uskrsnoj slavi.

magisterium.assessment_en: The third and fourth mysteries substantively correspond to the luminous mysteries: Jesus's proclamation of the Kingdom of God with the call to conversion and his Transfiguration, which according to tradition took place on Mount Tabor. The quotation regarding the kingdom and conversion appropriately summarizes Mk 1:15, but if intended as a verbatim biblical quotation, it omits the call to believe in the gospel.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Jesus's proclamation of the kingdom connects conversion with his works of mercy and forgiveness; conversion is therefore a response to God's coming, not merely a general change of behavior. The Transfiguration reveals Christ's glory, and the voice of the Father calls the disciples to listen to him, preparing them for the journey toward the passion and resurrection glory.
concerns_en: The quotation “Repent, the kingdom of God is at hand” is not a complete literal quotation of Mk 1:15: in the source, along with repentance, the call to believe in the gospel is also stated. This is a minor quotation imprecision, rather than an essential doctrinal deviation.

sections.subtitle_en: "Repent, the kingdom of God is at hand" and the light from Mount Tabor
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar announces the third mystery, the proclamation of the kingdom of God and the call to conversion
sections.content_en:
**The third mystery of light**, as announced by Vladimir Grebenar, is dedicated to Jesus who proclaimed: **"Repent, the kingdom of God is at hand."** The call to conversion in this mystery thematically connects directly to the gospel of the day with which the episode opened, the one about the joy of heaven over one repentant sinner. The Rosary thus continues the thread that connects all parts of the prayer.

Next follows the **fourth mystery**: Jesus, who **was transfigured on Mount Tabor**. In both mysteries, the host keeps to the established order. He prays the Our Father, ten Hail Marys, and Glory Be to the Father, and concludes each decade with the petition "O my Jesus, forgive us our sins", along with a prayer for the souls in most need of God's mercy.

sections.subtitle: Euharistija na Posljednjoj večeri i „Zdravo Kraljice“ kao završni pozdrav Majci milosrđa
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj zaključuje krunicu molitvom „Zdravo Kraljice“
sections.content:
Krunicu zaokružuje **peto otajstvo svjetla**: Isus, koji je **na Posljednjoj večeri ustanovio svetu euharistiju**. I ova desetica moli se istim redom kao i prethodne, a završava zazivom za milosrđe prema dušama kojima je ono najpotrebnije.

Za kraj molitvenog bloka Vladimir Grebenar izabire molitvu **„Zdravo Kraljice“**, u kojoj se Marija pozdravlja kao „majka milosrđa, život, slast i ufanje naše“. Vjernici se u njoj prepoznaju kao „prognani sinovi Evini“ koji joj vapiju i uzdišu, „tugujući i plačući u ovoj suznoj dolini“. Molitva traži da Marija, kao zagovornica, svrne svoje „milostive oči“ na njih te da im nakon ovoga progona pokaže Isusa, blagoslovljeni plod svoje utrobe.

Završnim usklikom **„O blaga, o mila, o slatka Djevice Marijo“** završava zajednička molitva koja je počela molitvom oslobođenja, a vodila je kroz posvete, krunicu i litanije Božanskom milosrđu te otajstva svjetla. Cijeli molitveni dio okupljen je oko jedne poruke: milosrđa kojim Bog traži i prihvaća svakog grešnika.

magisterium.assessment: Marijanski dio uglavnom je potpuno usklađen s katoličkim naukom: zazivanje Marije kao Majke milosrđa i zagovornice izražava njezinu majčinsku skrb, a ne zamjenjuje Krista. Tvrdnja o ustanovljenju Euharistije na Posljednjoj večeri katolički je nauk, ali dostavljeni izvori ne uključuju biblijski odlomak o tom događaju.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva uči da Marija svojim zagovorom pomaže vjernicima, ali njezina je uloga podređena jedinom posredništvu Krista i usmjerava vjernike k njemu. Zato zaziv „pokaži nam Isusa” dobro izražava katoličko razumijevanje marijanske pobožnosti.

magisterium.assessment_en: The Marian portion is mostly fully aligned with Catholic doctrine: invoking Mary as Mother of Mercy and advocate expresses her maternal care, rather than replacing Christ. The assertion regarding the institution of the Eucharist at the Last Supper is Catholic doctrine, but the provided sources do not include the biblical passage regarding that event.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church teaches that Mary helps the faithful through her intercession, but her role is subordinate to the unique mediation of Christ and directs believers to him. Therefore, the invocation “show unto us Jesus” expresses well the Catholic understanding of Marian devotion.

sections.subtitle_en: The Eucharist at the Last Supper and "Hail Holy Queen" as the final greeting to the Mother of Mercy
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host concludes the Rosary with the prayer "Hail Holy Queen"
sections.content_en:
The Rosary is rounded off by the **fifth mystery of light**: Jesus, who **instituted the Holy Eucharist at the Last Supper**. This decade is also prayed in the same order as the previous ones, and ends with an invocation for mercy toward the souls who are most in need of it.

For the conclusion of the prayer block, Vladimir Grebenar chooses the prayer **"Hail Holy Queen"**, in which Mary is greeted as "mother of mercy, our life, our sweetness, and our hope." The faithful recognize themselves in it as "poor banished children of Eve" who cry and sigh to her, "mourning and weeping in this valley of tears." The prayer asks that Mary, as an advocate, turn her "eyes of mercy" toward them and that after this exile she show them Jesus, the blessed fruit of her womb.

With the final exclamation **"O clement, o loving, o sweet Virgin Mary"**, the common prayer ends, which began with the prayer of deliverance, and led through consecrations, the chaplet and litany of Divine Mercy, and the mysteries of light. The entire prayer part is gathered around one message: the mercy with which God seeks and accepts every sinner.

sections.subtitle: „Mi smo obrezanje“: Pavlov odgovor na dičenje tijelom, nacijom i zakonom
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar započinje tumačenje Pavlovih riječi iz Poslanice Filipljanima
sections.content:
Nakon molitve krunice i Zdravo Kraljice, voditelj **Vladimir Grebenar** prelazi na tumačenje svete riječi iz **Poslanice Filipljanima**. Čita poznati odlomak u kojem sveti Pavao piše: „Braćo, mi smo obrezanje. Mi koji u Duhu Božjemu obavljamo bogoslužje i dičimo se Kristom Isusom, a ne pouzdajemo se u tijelo.“ Apostol zatim nabraja razloge zbog kojih bi se, kako sam kaže, mogao pouzdati u tijelo i više od drugih:

- obrezan osmoga dana,
- od roda Izraelova, plemena Benjaminova,
- Hebrej od Hebreja,
- po zakonu farizej,
- po revnosti progonitelj Crkve,
- po pravednosti zakonskoj besprijekoran.

Pavao ipak zaključuje: „Što mi god bijaše dobitak, to poradi Krista smatram gubitkom. Što više, čak sve gubitkom smatram zbog onoga najizvrsnijeg, zbog spoznanja Isusa Krista, Gospodina mojega.“

Grebenar se pita zašto apostol uopće spominje obrezanje. Objašnjava da su se Židovi hvalili time što su poseban narod. Vidljiv znak koji ih je na tijelu razlikovao od drugih naroda bilo je obrezanje muškaraca. Pritom ističe da nisu smatrali velikim sam čin obrezanja, nego **Mojsijev zakon** i način života koji iz njega proizlazi. Znak pripadnosti tom narodu nosili su na tijelu.

Prema voditelju, Židovi su se dičili nacijom: vjerovali su da su Božji narod, da nose znak Božje pripadnosti i da je svaki pojedinac član naroda koji je utemeljio sam Bog. Pavao tome suprotstavlja novu stvarnost: „obrezanje“ su sada oni koji žive u Duhu Božjem i diče se Isusom Kristom.

Grebenar to prenosi u današnje okolnosti. Hvaljenje u tijelu, kaže, bilo bi kad bi se netko dičio time što je Hrvat, katolik, što je završio visoku školu, ima uspješan posao ili karijeru. Sveti Pavao to naziva dičenjem tijelom. Kad netko misli da se može hvaliti na takav način, apostol odgovara da on može još više, pa nabraja svoja postignuća. Bio je besprijekoran farizej, vrlo učen čovjek koji je dosljedno živio zakon. Voditelj zaključuje da je upravo sve to bilo **zapreka da primi Isusa**.

magisterium.assessment: Tumačenje ispravno prenosi Pavlovu tvrdnju da se kršćani diče Kristom, a ne pouzdaju u tijelo, te da je zbog Krista svoje prijašnje dobitke smatrao gubitkom. Ipak, zaključak da su Pavlova židovska pripadnost, zakon i postignuća sami po sebi bili zapreka da primi Isusa pretjeruje u odnosu na tekst i može pogrešno prikazati židovsku baštinu.
concerns: Pavlov popis obrezanja, izraelskoga podrijetla i farizejskog života ne znači da su židovska pripadnost ili Mojsijev zakon sami po sebi bili prepreka vjeri; tekst naglašava da se Pavao više ne pouzdaje u takve prednosti kao osnovu opravdanja pred Bogom.

Primjena na hrvatsku, katoličku ili obrazovnu pripadnost zahtijeva razlikovanje: sama pripadnost ili postignuće nije nužno hvalisanje „tijelom”; problem je pouzdanje u njih umjesto u Krista. Pavlov zaključak govori o vrijednosti spoznanja Krista iznad prijašnjih dobitaka.
Opis Židova kao skupine koja se dičila nacijom preširoko generalizira i nije izravno potvrđen navedenim Pavlovim odlomkom.
magisterium.enrichment: Pavao navodi svoje naslijeđene i stečene prednosti kako bi pokazao da se ni on ne može hvaliti više od svojih protivnika; njegov je naglasak da nijedna od tih prednosti ne nadmašuje Krista. Stoga je prikladnije reći da je pogrešno pouzdanje u vlastiti status ili zasluge zapreka predanju Kristu, a ne da su nacionalna, vjerska ili osobna dobra sama po sebi zapreka.

magisterium.assessment_en: The interpretation correctly conveys Paul's assertion that Christians boast in Christ and do not rely on the flesh, and that for Christ's sake he considered his previous gains as loss. Nevertheless, the conclusion that Paul's Jewish belonging, the law, and achievements were in themselves an obstacle to receiving Jesus exaggerates in relation to the text and can misrepresent Jewish heritage.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Paul lists his inherited and acquired advantages in order to show that he, too, cannot boast more than his opponents; his emphasis is that none of those advantages surpasses Christ. It is therefore more appropriate to say that misguided reliance on one's own status or merits is an obstacle to surrender to Christ, rather than that national, religious, or personal goods are obstacles in themselves.
concerns_en: Paul's list of circumcision, Israelite heritage, and Pharisaic life does not mean that Jewish belonging or the Law of Moses were in themselves obstacles to faith; the text emphasizes that Paul no longer relies on such advantages as the basis of justification before God.

Application to Croatian, Catholic, or educational affiliation requires distinction: affiliation or achievement itself is not necessarily boasting in the “flesh”; the problem is reliance on them instead of on Christ. Paul's conclusion speaks of the value of knowing Christ above former gains.
Describing Jews as a group that boasted in nation overgeneralizes and is not directly supported by the cited Pauline passage.

sections.subtitle_en: "We are the circumcision": Paul's response to boasting in the flesh, nation, and law
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar begins the interpretation of Paul's words from the Epistle to the Philippians
sections.content_en:
After the prayer of the Rosary and Hail Holy Queen, host **Vladimir Grebenar** transitions to the interpretation of the holy word from the **Epistle to the Philippians**. He reads the well-known passage in which Saint Paul writes: "Brethren, we are the circumcision. We who worship in the Spirit of God and glory in Christ Jesus, and have no confidence in the flesh." The apostle then enumerates the reasons why, as he says himself, he could have confidence in the flesh even more than others:

- circumcised on the eighth day,
- of the race of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin,
- a Hebrew of Hebrews,
- as to the law, a Pharisee,
- as to zeal, a persecutor of the Church,
- as to righteousness under the law, blameless.

Yet Paul concludes: "Whatever was gain to me, that I counted loss for the sake of Christ. More than that, I count everything as loss because of the surpassing excellence of knowing Christ Jesus, my Lord."

Grebenar wonders why the apostle mentions circumcision at all. He explains that the Jews boasted of being a special people. The visible sign that distinguished them in the flesh from other nations was the circumcision of men. At the same time, he emphasizes that they did not consider great the mere act of circumcision, but the **Law of Moses** and the way of life arising from it. The sign of belonging to that nation they bore on their bodies.

According to the host, the Jews boasted in their nation: they believed that they were God's people, that they bore the sign of belonging to God, and that each individual was a member of a nation founded by God himself. Paul contrasts this with a new reality: the "circumcision" are now those who live in the Spirit of God and boast in Jesus Christ.

Grebenar transfers this into today's circumstances. Boasting in the flesh, he says, would be if someone boasted of being a Croat, a Catholic, having graduated from higher education, having a successful job or career. Saint Paul calls this boasting in the flesh. When someone thinks they can boast in such a manner, the apostle replies that he can do so even more, and then enumerates his achievements. He was a blameless Pharisee, a very learned man who lived the law consistently. The host concludes that all of this was precisely the **obstacle to receiving Jesus**.

sections.subtitle: Kad zasluge priječe milost: poziv da se ide na zadnje mjesto
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj upozorava da i dostignuća unutar Crkve mogu biti zapreka Božjoj milosti
sections.content:
Grebenar ističe da se Pavao, kad je shvatio da se pouzdavao u tijelo, zapravo pouzdavao u **svoja svjetovna dostignuća**. Dodaje važnu napomenu: takva dostignuća ne postoje samo u svijetu, nego i u Crkvi i u vjeri.

Kao primjer navodi osobu koja sebe vidi prvenstveno kao voditelja molitvene zajednice. Kada se netko tako doživljava, upozorava Grebenar, to **priječi djelovanje Božje milosti**.

Nudi i protulijek: „Najbolje je kad ništa ne očekuješ, pa te Bog postavi tamo gdje on želi.“ Savjetuje da se uvijek ide na zadnje mjesto i da se čovjek ne gura naprijed. Onaj tko sjedne na posljednje mjesto, kaže, biva od Boga postavljen na bolje.

Zato, prema njegovu tumačenju, sveti Pavao uči da se ne treba dičiti tijelom ni svjetovnim dostignućima. Pod tim voditelj nabraja fakultetske diplome, dobre automobile, stanove, kuće i karijere.

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak na poniznosti i odricanju od pouzdanja u vlastite zasluge dobro odgovara Pavlovu učenju da se vjernik hvali Kristom, a ne „tijelom“. Ipak, odlomak proširuje Pavlovu konkretnu kritiku vlastitih povlastica i zasluga u Fil 3 na sva svjetovna postignuća, a tvrdnje da identifikacija s voditeljskom ulogom priječi milost i da će Bog osobu sa zadnjeg mjesta postaviti na bolje mjesto mogu zvučati previše kategorično ili kao obećanje nagrade.
concerns: U Fil 3 Pavao govori o svojim etničkim i vjerskim povlasticama te o pouzdanju u vlastitu pravednost; njegova poanta nije da su diplome, imovina ili karijera sami po sebi zli, nego da ne mogu biti temelj opravdanja ni razlog za hvalisanje pred Bogom.

Upozorenje protiv toga da se netko prvenstveno poistovjeti s ulogom voditelja može biti duhovno korisno, ali tvrdnja da takav doživljaj „priječi djelovanje Božje milosti“ nije dovoljno razlučena: problem bi bio oholost ili samodostatnost, a ne sama služba ili odgovornost.

Savjet da se ide na posljednje mjesto podupire poniznost, ali tvrdnja da će takva osoba biti postavljena „na bolje“ može poniznost prikazati kao strategiju za dobivanje više časti, umjesto kao slobodno služenje Bogu i bližnjemu.
magisterium.enrichment: Pavao ne poriče da je imao ozbiljne vjerske i intelektualne povlastice; poriče da mu one daju razlog za pouzdanje neovisno o Kristu, kojega smatra neusporedivo većim dobitkom. Poniznost zato ne znači prezirati darove, obrazovanje ili službu, nego ih primati kao darove i ne pretvarati ih u mjerilo vlastite vrijednosti ili duhovne nadmoći.

Epistola ad sacram virginem Demetriadem, seu de humilitate tractatus (Letter to the holy virgin Demetrias, or a treatise on humility)

magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis on humility and renunciation of reliance on one's own merits corresponds well to Paul's teaching that the believer boasts in Christ, not in the “flesh.” Nevertheless, the passage extends Paul's concrete critique of his own privileges and merits in Phil 3 to all worldly achievements, and the claims that identification with a leadership role impedes grace and that God will place the person from the last place into a better place can sound overly categorical or like a promise of reward.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Paul does not deny that he had serious religious and intellectual privileges; he denies that they give him reason for confidence independently of Christ, whom he regards as an incomparably greater gain. Humility therefore does not mean despising gifts, education, or ministry, but receiving them as gifts and not turning them into the measure of one's own worth or spiritual superiority.
concerns_en: In Phil 3 Paul speaks of his ethnic and religious privileges and of reliance on his own righteousness; his point is not that degrees, property, or career are evil in themselves, but that they cannot be the foundation of justification or a reason for boasting before God.

The warning against identifying primarily with the role of a leader can be spiritually useful, but the claim that such a self-perception “impedes the action of God's grace” is not sufficiently distinguished: the problem would be pride or self-sufficiency, not ministry or responsibility itself.

The counsel to go to the last place supports humility, but the claim that such a person will be placed “in a better place” can present humility as a strategy for gaining more honor, instead of as free service to God and neighbor.

sections.subtitle_en: When merits hinder grace: a call to go to the lowest place
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host warns that achievements within the Church can also be an obstacle to God's grace
sections.content_en:
Grebenar emphasizes that Paul, when he realized he was putting confidence in the flesh, was actually relying on **his worldly achievements**. He adds an important observation: such achievements exist not only in the world, but also in the Church and in faith.

As an example, he mentions a person who views himself primarily as a leader of a prayer group. When someone perceives themselves that way, Grebenar warns, it **hinders the work of God's grace**.

He also offers an antidote: "It is best when you expect nothing, so God puts you where he wants." He advises always going to the lowest place and not pushing oneself forward. The one who sits in the lowest place, he says, is placed by God into a better one.

Therefore, according to his interpretation, Saint Paul teaches not to boast in the flesh or in worldly achievements. Under that, the host lists university degrees, good cars, apartments, houses, and careers.

sections.subtitle: Isus na prvom mjestu: kad znanje postaje Božje oružje
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar govori o svom profesionalnom putu i početku navještanja evanđelja
sections.content:
Umjesto svjetovnih postignuća, naglašava Grebenar, dičiti se treba **Isusom Kristom**. Kad je Krist na prvom mjestu i kad ga vjernici navješćuju, sve što su stekli „u tijelu“ podredi se Bogu i on to iskoristi.

Kao primjer opet uzima Pavla. Apostol nije izgubio znanje o Mojsijevu zakonu i Starom zavjetu. Kad se krstio i primio Duha Svetoga, cijelo to znanje počeo je koristiti za evangelizaciju. „Tek tada je naučio kako treba znati“, ističe voditelj. Pavao se nije odrekao znanja koje je stjecao desetljećima. Upravo je tada, kad je Isusa stavio na prvo mjesto, to znanje postalo **Božje oružje** kojim je obratio mnoge ljude.

Grebenar zatim dijeli osobno iskustvo, o kojem je, kako kaže, govorio i dan ranije na jednom od skupova koje svakodnevno održava. U svojoj je struci dugo rastao osobno i profesionalno. Došao je do točke na kojoj je za jednu osobu imao „puno škole, puno ekspertize“. Tek tada je počeo navještati evanđelje. Prema njegovim riječima, Gospodin ga je tada upotrijebio, pa se sada i znanje iz njegove struke koristi za obraćenje drugih i za Božje pothvate. Kao jedan takav pothvat navodi **domoljubnu inicijativu Ora et Labora**.

Poruku sažima ovako: ono što se nauči vlastitim trudom, kroz školovanje i rad, Bog na najbolji način iskoristi kad se Isusa stavi na prvo mjesto. Za to je, upozorava, potrebna **strpljivost s Bogom**, jer Bog radi na duge staze, a ne na kratke.

magisterium.assessment: Središnja poruka da Krist mora biti iznad ljudskog znanja i postignuća, a da se darovi mogu staviti u službu naviještanja, uglavnom je u skladu s katoličkim naukom: Pavao poznaje i naviješta Krista kao najveći dobitak, dok se Sveto pismo i poznavanje Zakona mogu koristiti kao duhovna sredstva. Ipak, osobno iskustvo voditelja i opis Pavlova razvoja treba shvatiti kao svjedočanstvo i duhovnu primjenu, a ne kao opće pravilo da se znanje u punini koristi tek nakon određenog trenutka obraćenja.
concerns: Izraz „Božje oružje“ može biti prikladna slika za znanje stavljeno u službu evanđelja, ali ne bi ga trebalo razumjeti kao da su ljudska stručnost ili retorička sposobnost same po sebi izvor obraćenja. Katolički nauk razlikuje korisnost studija od novoga života milosti, koji studij sam ne proizvodi.

Odlomak Pavlovu uporabu poznavanja Zakona i Staroga zavjeta prikazuje uvjerljivo, ali sažeto; Fil 3 naglašava i da Pavao svoje ranije dobitke smatra gubitkom u usporedbi s Kristom, a ne samo da ih nastavlja koristiti na novi način.
magisterium.enrichment: Pavao izričito povezuje svoje poznavanje Zakona s naviještanjem evanđelja, a crkveno tumačenje Svetoga pisma ističe kako je bio „naoružan duhovnim oružjem“ te je starozavjetne spise stavljao u službu Krista. Istodobno, susret s Kristom mijenja srce i usmjerava život, dok obrazovanje može pomoći naviještanju, ali ne zamjenjuje obraćenje, molitvu ni djelovanje milosti.

magisterium.assessment_en: The central message that Christ must be above human knowledge and achievements, and that gifts can be placed at the service of proclamation, is mainly in accordance with Catholic doctrine: Paul knows and proclaims Christ as the greatest gain, while Sacred Scripture and knowledge of the Law can be used as spiritual means. Nevertheless, the personal experience of the leader and the description of Paul's development should be understood as a testimony and spiritual application, rather than as a general rule that knowledge is utilized in fullness only after a specific moment of conversion.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Paul explicitly connects his knowledge of the Law with the proclamation of the gospel, and the Church's interpretation of Sacred Scripture points out how he was “armed with spiritual weapons” and placed Old Testament writings at the service of Christ. At the same time, the encounter with Christ changes the heart and directs life, while education can assist proclamation, but does not replace conversion, prayer, or the working of grace.
concerns_en: The phrase “God's weapon” can be an appropriate metaphor for knowledge placed at the service of the gospel, but it should not be understood as if human expertise or rhetorical ability were in themselves the source of conversion. Catholic doctrine distinguishes the usefulness of studies from the new life of grace, which study alone does not produce.

The passage presents Paul's use of the knowledge of the Law and the Old Testament convincingly, but concisely; Phil 3 also emphasizes that Paul regards his earlier gains as loss in comparison with Christ, and not merely that he continues to use them in a new way.

sections.subtitle_en: Jesus in first place: when knowledge becomes God's weapon
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar speaks about his professional journey and the beginning of proclaiming the gospel
sections.content_en:
Instead of worldly achievements, Grebenar emphasizes, one should boast in **Jesus Christ**. When Christ is in first place and when the faithful proclaim him, everything they acquired "in the flesh" is subordinated to God and he utilizes it.

As an example, he again takes Paul. The apostle did not lose his knowledge of the Law of Moses and the Old Testament. When he was baptized and received the Holy Spirit, he began to use all that knowledge for evangelization. "Only then did he learn how one ought to know," the host emphasizes. Paul did not renounce the knowledge he had acquired over decades. It was precisely then, when he put Jesus in first place, that this knowledge became **God's weapon** by which he converted many people.

Grebenar then shares personal experience, about which, as he says, he spoke the day before at one of the gatherings he holds daily. In his profession, he grew personally and professionally for a long time. He reached a point where, for one person, he had "a lot of schooling, a lot of expertise." Only then did he begin to proclaim the gospel. According to his words, the Lord used him then, and now the knowledge from his profession is also used for the conversion of others and for God's endeavors. As one such endeavor, he cites the **patriotic initiative Ora et Labora**.

He summarizes the message like this: what is learned through one's own effort, through schooling and work, God uses in the best way when Jesus is put in first place. For that, he warns, **patience with God** is necessary, because God works for the long haul, not the short.

sections.subtitle: Psalam radosti i prispodobe o izgubljenoj ovci i drahmi
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj čita evanđelje o pastiru koji ostavlja 99 ovaca kako bi pronašao izgubljenu
sections.content:
Nakon tumačenja poslanice Grebenar čita psalam s pripjevom **„Neka se raduje srce onih što traže Gospodina“**. Psalam poziva na pjesmu i sviranje Gospodinu, pripovijedanje njegovih čudesa i dičenje njegovim svetim imenom. Poziva i da se svagda traži Gospodina, njegova snaga i lice. Spominje Abrahamov rod i sinove Jakovljeve kao Gospodnje izabranike te završava riječima: „On je Gospodin Bog naš. Po svoj su zemlji njegovi sudovi.“

Slijedi evanđelje. Oko Isusa okupljaju se carinici i grešnici kako bi ga slušali, dok farizeji i pismoznanci mrmljaju: „Ovaj prima grešnike i blaguje s njima.“ Isus im odgovara dvjema prispodobama.

U prvoj čovjek ima sto ovaca i izgubi jednu. Ostavlja devedeset i devet u pustinji i traži izgubljenu dok je ne nađe. Kad je pronađe, radostan je stavlja na ramena, saziva prijatelje i susjede i kaže: „Radujte se sa mnom, nađoh ovcu svoju izgubljenu.“ Isus zaključuje da će na nebu biti **veća radost zbog jednog obraćena grešnika** nego zbog devedeset i devet pravednika kojima ne treba obraćenja.

Druga prispodoba govori o ženi koja ima deset drahmi i izgubi jednu. Zapali svjetiljku, pomete kuću i brižno je traži dok je ne nađe. Kad je nađe, poziva prijateljice i susjede da se raduju s njom. „Tako, kažem vam, biva radost pred anđelima Božjim zbog jednog obraćena grešnika.“

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je vrlo usklađen sa Svetim pismom: vjerno prenosi Lk 15,1–10, uključujući Isusov odgovor na prigovor farizeja i pismoznanaca te radost zbog grešnika koji se obraća. Naglasak na Božjoj potrazi za izgubljenim i nebeskoj radosti zbog obraćenja odgovara katoličkom tumačenju Božjeg milosrđa.
magisterium.enrichment: Prispodobe ne opravdavaju grijeh, nego pokazuju Božju inicijativu i radost kada se grešnik vrati Bogu; obraćenje ostaje bitan dio poruke. Lukino 15. poglavlje nastavlja se prispodobom o milosrdnom ocu, koja dodatno prikazuje Božje milosrđe i poziv na povratak.
