magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is very aligned with Sacred Scripture: it faithfully conveys Lk 15:1–10, including Jesus's response to the objection of the Pharisees and scribes and the joy over the sinner who repents. The emphasis on God's search for the lost and heavenly joy over conversion corresponds to the Catholic interpretation of God's mercy.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The parables do not justify sin, but show God's initiative and joy when a sinner returns to God; conversion remains an essential part of the message. The 15th chapter of Luke continues with the parable of the prodigal father, which further illustrates God's mercy and the call to return.

sections.subtitle_en: Psalm of joy and parables of the lost sheep and the drachma
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host reads the gospel about the shepherd who leaves 99 sheep to find the lost one
sections.content_en:
After the interpretation of the epistle, Grebenar reads a psalm with the response **"Let the hearts of those who seek the Lord rejoice"**. The psalm calls for singing and making music to the Lord, recounting his wondrous deeds, and glorying in his holy name. It also calls to seek the Lord always, his strength and his face. It mentions the offspring of Abraham and the sons of Jacob as the Lord's chosen ones, and concludes with the words: "He is the Lord our God. In all the earth are his judgments."

The gospel follows. Tax collectors and sinners gather around Jesus to hear him, while Pharisees and scribes murmur: "This man welcomes sinners and eats with them." Jesus answers them with two parables.

In the first, a man has a hundred sheep and loses one. He leaves the ninety-nine in the desert and searches for the lost one until he finds it. When he finds it, he joyfully sets it on his shoulders, gathers his friends and neighbors, and says: "Rejoice with me, for I have found my lost sheep." Jesus concludes that there will be **greater joy in heaven over one repentant sinner** than over ninety-nine righteous persons who need no repentance.

The second parable speaks of a woman who has ten drachmas and loses one. She lights a lamp, sweeps the house, and diligently searches until she finds it. When she finds it, she invites female friends and neighbors to rejoice with her. "Just so, I tell you, there is joy before the angels of God over one repentant sinner."

sections.subtitle: Isusova misija: obraćenje grešnika, silazak nad pakao i čistilište
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj objašnjava silazak Krista u podzemlje i oslobođenje duša pravednika
sections.content:
Tumačeći evanđelje, Grebenar ističe da Isus njime želi naglasiti da je **obraćenje grešnika** misija zbog koje je došao na zemlju. Vjernici bi, kaže, to trebali posvijestiti.

Ključni razlog Isusova dolaska, prema voditelju, jest da se ljudi obrate, da vjeruju u jedinorođenoga Sina Božjega i da se svijet spasi. Svrha nije osuda grešnika i njihovo bacanje u pakao, nego spasenje.

Objašnjava i da prije Isusa pravednici nisu mogli uzaći na nebo. Nakon smrti na križu Krist je sašao u podzemlje i oslobodio duše pravednika da odu u raj. Grebenar predviđa pitanje kako su se duše pravednika uopće našle u podzemlju i odgovara: grijeha su imali svi, pa i pravednici. „Nema nikoga tko nije imao grijeha. Nema danas nikoga tko je bez grijeha.“

Budući da u nebo ne može ući ništa nečisto, pojašnjava voditelj, i mali grijesi koji su „zaprljali naše haljine“ razlog su zbog kojeg čovjek ne može odmah ući u raj, nego mora ostati u **čistilištu**.

Isusovu misiju zatim povezuje s njegovim riječima: „Nisam došao zvati pravednike, nego grešnike. Ne treba zdravima liječnik, nego bolesnima.“ Zaključuje da je **Isus liječnik**, a prispodoba o pastiru koji se raduje pronađenoj ovci više nego devedeset i devet onih u toru izražava upravo tu poruku.

magisterium.assessment: Glavna tvrdnja da Krist poziva grešnike, donosi spasenje i raduje se njihovu obraćenju u skladu je s evanđeoskom porukom; također je katolički nauk da je Krist svojim silaskom među mrtve otvorio pravednicima koji su ga čekali put u blaženstvo. Ipak, izjave o grijehu svih ljudi i čistilištu traže preciznije formuliranje, a izraz „podzemlje” ne bi smio sugerirati da su pravednici bili u istom stanju kao osuđeni.
concerns: Tvrdnja da „nema nikoga tko nije imao grijeha” ne smije se razumjeti kao beziznimna: Isus je bez grijeha, a katolički nauk uči da je Marija bila očuvana od istočnoga grijeha. Bolje je reći da su svi ljudi, osim Krista, podložni grijehu, uz posebnu milost koja je sačuvala Mariju.
Silazak u podzemlje treba razlikovati od silaska u pakao osuđenih: Krist je sišao među mrtve kako bi oslobodio pravednike koji su čekali Otkupitelja, a ne da bi spasio osuđene.

Objašnjenje čistilišta pojednostavljeno je ako se kaže da su „mali grijesi” sami po sebi razlog zbog kojega čovjek mora ostati ondje. Čistilište je konačno očišćenje onih koji umiru u Božjoj milosti, ali još nisu potpuno očišćeni; nije drugo odredište nakon smrti niti prilika za obraćenje.
Tvrdnju da Isus nije došao osuditi nego spasiti treba razumjeti kao naglasak na njegovoj spasiteljskoj misiji, a ne kao poricanje suda ili mogućnosti konačnog odbacivanja Boga.
magisterium.enrichment: U Lk 15 Isus objavljuje Božje milosrđe prema grešniku, ali prispodobe istodobno govore o obraćenju, a ne o spasenju neovisno o obraćenju. Katolički nauk razlikuje Abrahamovo krilo, gdje su pravednici čekali Krista, od pakla osuđenih; Kristov silazak dovršava djelo spasenja za pravednike, a ne ukida osudu onih koji su konačno odbacili Boga.

"He Descended Into Hell": The Theology of Hans Urs von Balthasar and Catholic Doctrine

magisterium.assessment_en: The main assertion that Christ calls sinners, brings salvation, and rejoices over their conversion is in accordance with the gospel message; it is also Catholic doctrine that Christ, by his descent among the dead, opened the way to beatitude for the righteous who were awaiting him. Nevertheless, the statements about the sinfulness of all human beings and purgatory require more precise formulation, and the term “underworld” should not suggest that the righteous were in the same state as the damned.
magisterium.enrichment_en: In Lk 15 Jesus reveals God's mercy toward the sinner, but the parables simultaneously speak of conversion, and not of salvation independent of conversion. Catholic doctrine distinguishes the Bosom of Abraham, where the righteous were awaiting Christ, from the hell of the damned; Christ's descent completes the work of salvation for the righteous, rather than annulling the damnation of those who have definitively rejected God.
concerns_en: The claim that “there is no one who did not have sin” must not be understood as without exception: Jesus is without sin, and Catholic doctrine teaches that Mary was preserved from original sin. It is better to say that all people, except Christ, are subject to sin, with the special grace that preserved Mary.

The descent into the underworld must be distinguished from the descent into the hell of the damned: Christ descended among the dead in order to free the righteous who were awaiting the Redeemer, and not to save the damned.

The explanation of purgatory is oversimplified if it is said that “small sins” are in themselves the reason why a person must remain there. Purgatory is the final purification of those who die in God's grace, but are not yet fully cleansed; it is not another destination after death nor an opportunity for conversion.

The claim that Jesus did not come to condemn but to save should be understood as an emphasis on his salvific mission, and not as a denial of judgment or the possibility of definitive rejection of God.

sections.subtitle_en: Jesus' mission: conversion of sinners, descent into hell, and purgatory
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host explains the descent of Christ into the underworld and the liberation of the souls of the righteous
sections.content_en:
Interpreting the gospel, Grebenar emphasizes that Jesus through it wants to stress that the **conversion of sinners** is the mission for which he came to earth. The faithful, he says, should become conscious of this.

The key reason for Jesus' coming, according to the host, is that people convert, believe in the only-begotten Son of God, and that the world be saved. The purpose is not condemnation of sinners and casting them into hell, but salvation.

He also explains that before Jesus, the righteous could not ascend to heaven. After his death on the cross, Christ descended into the underworld and liberated the souls of the righteous so they could go to heaven. Grebenar anticipates the question of how the souls of the righteous found themselves in the underworld in the first place and answers: everyone had sins, even the righteous. "There is no one who did not have sin. Today there is no one who is without sin."

Since nothing unclean can enter heaven, the host clarifies, even small sins that "soiled our garments" are the reason why a person cannot immediately enter heaven, but must remain in **purgatory**.

He then connects Jesus' mission with his words: "I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners. Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick." He concludes that **Jesus is a physician**, and the parable of the shepherd who rejoices over the found sheep more than the ninety-nine in the fold expresses precisely that message.

sections.subtitle: Test vjere: raduješ li se kad drugi obrate grešnika?
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar postavlja gledateljima pitanje o radosti zbog tuđeg uspjeha u evangelizaciji
sections.content:
Iz prispodobe o ženi koja pronalazi drahmu i poziva prijateljice da se raduju s njom Grebenar izvodi pitanje koje je, priznaje, mnogo puta postavio i sebi: **„Radujem li se ja obraćenju grešnika preko drugih ljudi?“**

Konkretizira ga: kad čuje da je neki svećenik ili laik nekoga obratio i priveo Kristu, raduje li se tome iskreno? Anđeli se tome raduju, raduju se sveti i raduje se Presveto Trojstvo. Ako se netko tome ne raduje, kaže voditelj, to otkriva kakva je on osoba: da nije dobra, nego zla osoba.

Razlika je prema njemu jasna. Zli ljudi ne raduju se obraćenju grešnika, a dobri se raduju. Isus je došao obratiti grešnike, pa radost zbog obraćenja zapravo je radost zbog samoga Isusa. „Isus je naša radost“, naglašava.

Vjernicima zato predlaže da si postave taj **test**. To je, kaže, jedan od kriterija po kojem svatko može ocijeniti kakva je njegova vjera.

magisterium.assessment: Radost zbog obraćenja grešnika vjerno izražava Isusovu poruku u prispodobama o izgubljenoj drahmi i ovci te je u skladu s evanđeoskim pozivom na obraćenje. Ipak, zaključak da je svatko tko se ne raduje „zla osoba” previše je kategoričan: može opisati ozbiljan duhovni problem, ali sama odsutnost vidljive radosti ne omogućuje siguran sud o nečijem karakteru ili vjeri.
concerns: Oštra podjela na „dobre” koji se raduju i „zle” koji se ne raduju može nepravedno svesti osobu na jedan osjećaj ili trenutnu reakciju.
Radost zbog obraćenja može biti koristan poticaj za ispit savjesti, ali nije samostalni ili konačni test vjere.
magisterium.enrichment: Isus u Lk 15 prikazuje radost zbog povratka izgubljenoga kao odraz Božjeg milosrđa; crkveni oci također izričito povezuju tu radost s anđelima i obraćenjem grešnika. Takvo ispitivanje savjesti najbolje vodi poniznosti: ako primijetimo zavist ili ravnodušnost, pozvani smo tražiti obraćenje i rasti u ljubavi, a ne donositi konačan sud o sebi ili drugima.
magisterium.assessment_en: Joy over the conversion of a sinner faithfully expresses Jesus's message in the parables of the lost coin and sheep and is in accordance with the evangelical call to conversion. Nevertheless, the conclusion that anyone who does not rejoice is an “evil person” is overly categorical: it can describe a serious spiritual problem, but the mere absence of visible joy does not enable a certain judgment about someone's character or faith.
magisterium.enrichment_en: In Lk 15 Jesus presents joy over the return of the lost as a reflection of God's mercy; the Church Fathers also explicitly connect this joy with the angels and the conversion of sinners. Such an examination of conscience best leads to humility: if we notice envy or indifference, we are called to seek conversion and grow in love, rather than pass definitive judgment on ourselves or others.
concerns_en: The sharp division into the “good” who rejoice and the “evil” who do not rejoice can unjustly reduce a person to a single emotion or temporary reaction.
Joy over conversion can be a useful incentive for an examination of conscience, but it is not a standalone or definitive test of faith.

sections.subtitle_en: Test of faith: do you rejoice when others convert a sinner?
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar poses a question to viewers about rejoicing over another's success in evangelization
sections.content_en:
From the parable of the woman who finds the drachma and calls her friends to rejoice with her, Grebenar draws a question that, he admits, he has asked himself many times: **"Do I rejoice over the conversion of a sinner through other people?"**

He makes it concrete: when he hears that some priest or layperson converted someone and brought them to Christ, does he honestly rejoice over that? The angels rejoice over it, the saints rejoice, and the Most Holy Trinity rejoices. If someone does not rejoice over that, the host says, it reveals what kind of person he is: that he is not a good person, but an evil person.

The difference according to him is clear. Evil people do not rejoice over the conversion of sinners, and good people do rejoice. Jesus came to convert sinners, so joy over conversion is actually joy over Jesus himself. "Jesus is our joy," he emphasizes.

He therefore suggests to the faithful to give themselves that **test**. That is, he says, one of the criteria by which everyone can assess what kind of faith they have.

sections.subtitle: Kraće razmatranje zbog turneje: Pazin, Umag, Valpovo, Nova Gradiška, Bjelovar i Samobor
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj najavljuje raspored promocija knjige i predstavljanja domoljubne inicijative
sections.content:
Grebenar ovdje završava tumačenje i moli gledatelje za malo „kredita“. Objašnjava da zbog vrlo intenzivnog tempa promocija i predstavljanja inicijative trenutačno ne može tumačiti duže. Ipak ne želi uskratiti molitvu i tumačenje riječi, pa je razmatranje kraće. Vjeruje da je mnogima i to dovoljno jer nastoji naglasiti bitne stvari. Vjernike koji prate emisiju potiče da sami više mole, razmatraju i „druže se s Isusom“.

Slijedi najava promocija knjige i predstavljanja **domoljubne inicijative**:

- **Pazin**, petak, 6. studenoga, hotel Lovac, Šime Kurelića 4. Program počinje u 19 sati krunicom i uvodnom riječi, a samo predstavljanje knjige predviđeno je oko 20 sati.
- **Umag**, subota, 7. studenoga, hotel Garden Istra, Katoro.
- **Valpovo**, utorak, 10. studenoga, Vila Valpovo, Bana Josipa Jelačića 1.
- **Nova Gradiška**, srijeda, 11. studenoga, Centar kompetencija, Industrijska ulica 23/1.
- **Bjelovar**, četvrtak, 12. studenoga, Tehnološki park Bjelovar, Trg hrvatskih branitelja 14.
- **Samobor**, petak, 13. studenoga, hotel Lavica, Ferde Livadića 7.

Voditelj posebno moli gledatelje iz Istre, s područja Umaga i Pazina i okolice, da banner s Facebook stranice Ora et Labora podijele na svojim društvenim mrežama i pozovu one kojima bi to moglo koristiti. Poziva da svatko tko sluša, posti i moli pozove i dovede barem jednu osobu. Ako se ta osoba obrati, kaže, „tebi se računa u pravednost“. Najavljuje i da će sljedećeg dana objaviti nastavak rasporeda.

magisterium.assessment: Poziv na molitvu, razmatranje, druženje s Isusom i osobno svjedočenje evanđelja u skladu je s katoličkim poslanjem evangelizacije, a sam opis ne pokazuje prisilu prema pozvanima. Izraz da se obraćenje druge osobe pozivatelju „računa u pravednost” traži pojašnjenje: dobar je trud evangelizatora, ali tuđe obraćenje nije automatska zasluga koja se pripisuje pozivatelju niti je čovjekov doprinos zamjena za Božje djelovanje.
concerns: Formulacija „tebi se računa u pravednost” može se shvatiti kao da je obraćenje druge osobe zasluga ili pravednost koju pozivatelj stječe automatski; sadržaj to ne objašnjava.
Poticanje da se dovede barem jedna osoba treba ostati slobodan poziv i svjedočenje, bez pritiska ili neprimjerenog uvjeravanja.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkveni nauk opisuje obraćenje kao promjenu mišljenja i djelovanja te kao trajni rast u poistovjećenju s Kristom, na koji su pozvani i krštenici. Evangelizator sudjeluje u Kristovoj ljubavi i može naviještati osobnim svjedočanstvom, ali riječ i život trebaju biti povezani, a vjera se ne smije nametati prisilom ili neprimjerenim pritiskom.

magisterium.assessment_en: The call to prayer, meditation, spending time with Jesus, and personal witnessing to the gospel is in accordance with the Catholic mission of evangelization, and the description itself does not show coercion toward those invited. The expression that another person's conversion is “counted as righteousness” to the one who invites requires clarification: the evangelizer's effort is good, but someone else's conversion is not an automatic merit attributed to the caller, nor is human contribution a substitute for God's action.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Church teaching describes conversion as a change of mind and action, and as ongoing growth in identification with Christ, to which the baptized are also called. The evangelizer participates in Christ's love and can proclaim through personal testimony, but word and life should be joined, and faith must not be imposed through coercion or inappropriate pressure.
concerns_en: The phrasing “it is counted to you as righteousness” can be understood as if another person's conversion were a merit or righteousness that the inviter acquires automatically; the content does not explain this.
Encouragement to bring at least one person should remain a free invitation and testimony, without pressure or inappropriate persuasion.

sections.subtitle: Članstvo, donacije i portal Ora et Labora: od geopolitike do sporta
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar predstavlja portal Ora et Labora i poziva na čitanje
sections.content:
Grebenar zatim poziva gledatelje da postanu **članovi domoljubne inicijative Ora et Labora** tako što će ispuniti obrazac na mrežnoj stranici inicijative. Navodi i da su na ekranu brojevi mobitela suradnika iz Hrvatske i Bosne i Hercegovine, koje zainteresirani mogu nazvati za dodatne informacije.

Zahvaljuje svima koji podržavaju i doniraju inicijativu. Ističe da je to vrlo važno jer se pokreću, kako kaže, veliki i važni projekti za hrvatski narod u Hrvatskoj, u Bosni i Hercegovini i svugdje drugdje.

Posebno predstavlja **portal Ora et Labora**, koji je, prema njegovim riječima, „sve bolji i bolji“. Priznaje da bi mogao djelovati pristrano jer je i sam dio organizacije. Ipak tvrdi da bi i kao promatrator sa strane smatrao da na portalu ima što pročitati i naučiti. Kaže da je portal „digao“ razinu i da dnevno donosi mnogo objava i kvalitetnih tekstova.

Naglašava da to **nije vjerski portal** u užem smislu. Duhovnosti ima dosta i pišu i svećenici, ali cilj je donijeti istinu iz svih područja ljudskog života:

- politike i geopolitike,
- domaće politike,
- sporta,
- kulture i umjetnosti,
- povijesti.

Poziv na donacije ponavlja i ističe da su dobrodošli i mali iznosi od 5 ili 10 eura, uplaćeni kad se tko sjeti. Podsjeća vjernike na ono što im je Gospodin dao kroz zajedničke molitve i postove i zaključuje: „Dižemo nešto veliko na slavu Božju.“

magisterium.assessment: Poziv na članstvo i donacije te predstavljanje portala sami po sebi ne proturječe katoličkom nauku; domoljublje i rad za dobro naroda mogu biti legitimni, ako ostanu podređeni kršćanskim moralnim načelima i općem dobru. Budući da odlomak ne iznosi konkretne političke tvrdnje ni sadržaj navedenih projekata, njihovu činjeničnu točnost ili katoličku usklađenost nije moguće procijeniti.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk priznaje posebnu dužnost prema domovini, ali je stavlja nakon dužnosti prema Bogu, pa domoljublje ne opravdava postupke protiv moralnog zakona. Crkveni tekstovi također povezuju katoličku vjeru s odgovornim građanstvom i odanošću legitimnoj vlasti, a ne s poistovjećivanjem vjere s određenom političkom inicijativom.
magisterium.assessment_en: The call for membership and donations, as well as the presentation of the portal, do not in themselves contradict Catholic doctrine; patriotism and working for the good of the people can be legitimate, if they remain subordinate to Christian moral principles and the common good. Since the passage does not present specific political claims or the content of the mentioned projects, their factual accuracy or Catholic alignment cannot be evaluated.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic doctrine acknowledges a special duty toward one's homeland, but places it after duty toward God, so patriotism does not justify actions against the moral law. Church texts also connect the Catholic faith with responsible citizenship and loyalty to legitimate authority, rather than with identifying faith with a specific political initiative.

sections.subtitle_en: Membership, donations, and the Ora et Labora portal: from geopolitics to sports
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar presents the Ora et Labora portal and invites reading
sections.content_en:
Grebenar then invites viewers to become **members of the patriotic initiative Ora et Labora** by filling out the form on the initiative's website. He also states that the mobile phone numbers of associates from Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina are on the screen, whom interested parties can call for additional information.

He thanks everyone who supports and donates to the initiative. He emphasizes that this is very important because large and important projects, as he says, are being launched for the Croatian people in Croatia, in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and everywhere else.

He especially presents the **portal Ora et Labora**, which is, according to his words, "better and better". He admits that he might seem biased because he is also part of the organization. Yet he claims that even as an outside observer he would consider that there is something to read and learn on the portal. He says that the portal has "raised" its level and that it daily brings many posts and quality texts.

He stresses that this is **not a religious portal** in the narrow sense. There is plenty of spirituality and priests write too, but the goal is to bring the truth from all areas of human life:

- politics and geopolitics,
- domestic politics,
- sports,
- culture and art,
- history.

He repeats the call for donations and emphasizes that even small amounts of 5 or 10 euros are welcome, paid whenever one remembers. He reminds the faithful of what the Lord gave them through common prayers and fasts and concludes: "We are raising something great to the glory of God."

sections.subtitle: Ivankino svjedočanstvo: narkolepsija, post i poruka da se ne pouzdaje u čovjeka
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj čita Ivankino svjedočanstvo o nestanku simptoma narkolepsije i katapleksije
sections.content:
U dijelu posvećenom ozdravljenjima Grebenar čita svjedočanstvo gledateljice **Ivanke**. Ona piše da od posta i molitve s Ora et Labora nema simptoma **narkolepsije i katapleksije**.

Ivanka navodi da je u dogovoru s neurologinjom iz Zagreba odavno prestala uzimati lijekove. Ipak je i dalje znala osjećati umor nakon jela i blage simptome katapleksije. Od bolesti pati od sedmog razreda osnovne škole, a sada ima 33 godine. Oboljelima od narkolepsije i katapleksije preporučuje da pročitaju odlomak o padavičaru iz **Evanđelja po Marku, 9. poglavlje, retci 14 do 29**, s Isusovim riječima: „Ovaj se rod ničim drugim ne može izagnati osim molitvom i postom.“

Dodaje da tijekom posta može normalno funkcionirati, ali uvijek u molitvi dobro osluškuje je li pozvana na neki post ili nije. Svjedočanstvo završava rečenicom: „Ne častim i ne slavim Vladimira, nego Isusa Krista, Oca i Duha Svetoga.“ Vladimira, piše, smatra običnim čovjekom koji životom želi vršiti volju Očevu i koji vjernike često potiče na molitvu, pomoć i poslušnost Crkvi.

Grebenar je oduševljen. „Bravo. Kako si ovo lijepo napisala“, kaže, posebno hvaleći završni dio. Na tome gradi poruku: **nikad se ne treba pouzdavati u čovjeka**. Čovjek može iznevjeriti i razočarati, a Isus nikada. Otvoreno priznaje da i on sam može razočarati ljude. Kao primjer navodi Judu, koji je tri i pol godine bio s Isusom, a zatim ga izdao.

Zaključak je u skladu s naslovom epizode. Ljudi mogu razočarati jedni druge, ali Isus i Blažena Djevica Marija nikada. Zato **Isus mora biti na prvom mjestu, i onda će sve doći na svoje mjesto**.

magisterium.assessment: Svjedočanstvo o molitvi, postu i poboljšanju simptoma može se iznijeti kao osobno iskustvo, a molitva za tjelesno zdravlje pripada katoličkom životu; ipak, odlomak mora jasno razlikovati svjedočanstvo od dokazanog ozdravljenja i ne smije stvarati dojam da post liječi narkolepsiju ili katapleksiju. Poruka da je Isus prvi oslonac kršćanski je usmjerena, ali formulacija o Mariji i ljudima traži pojašnjenje kako se Marijino zagovorništvo ne bi izjednačilo s Kristom niti ljudsko povjerenje odbacilo kao takvo.
concerns: Isusov izgon zloduha u Marku 9 ne daje osnovu da se narkolepsija ili katapleksija tumače kao demonsko djelovanje ili da se taj odlomak preporuči kao terapija za te bolesti. U priloženom prijevodu retku 29 stoji da se takav duh može izagnati samo molitvom; podcastov navod dodaje post, što se ne podudara s tim prijevodom.

Ako se svjedočanstvo o nestanku simptoma prenosi kao potvrda čudesnog ozdravljenja ili kao obećanje drugima, to bi zahtijevalo opreznu provjeru i ne bi smjelo zamijeniti liječničku procjenu ni liječenje. Crkva potiče molitvu za zdravlje, ali istodobno naglašava da se ne odriče svakodnevne skrbi i liječenja bolesnih.

Izraz da se nikada ne treba pouzdavati u čovjeka može biti pretjerano širok: kršćansko pouzdanje u Boga ne isključuje razumno povjerenje, suradnju i traženje pomoći od drugih ljudi. Isus i Marija također nisu na istoj razini: Marija je stvorenje i zagovornica, dok je Krist jedini Spasitelj.
magisterium.enrichment: U Markovu izvještaju središnji je naglasak na Isusovoj vlasti, molitvi i ranjivoj vjeri oca koji moli: „Vjerujem; pomozi mojoj nevjeri!”; tekst ne poistovjećuje dječakovo stanje s današnjom dijagnozom narkolepsije. Katolička molitva za ozdravljenje može ići uz medicinsku skrb, a pojedinačno svjedočanstvo samo po sebi ne utvrđuje ni uzrok poboljšanja ni čudesno ozdravljenje.

magisterium.assessment_en: Testimony about prayer, fasting, and improvement of symptoms can be presented as personal experience, and prayer for physical health belongs to Catholic life; nevertheless, the passage must clearly distinguish testimony from proven healing and must not create the impression that fasting cures narcolepsy or cataplexy. The message that Jesus is the first support is Christianly directed, but the formulation regarding Mary and people requires clarification so that Mary's intercession is not equated with Christ, nor human trust rejected as such.
magisterium.enrichment_en: In Mark's account, the central emphasis is on Jesus's authority, prayer, and the vulnerable faith of the father who pleads: “I believe; help my unbelief!”; the text does not equate the boy's condition with today's diagnosis of narcolepsy. Catholic prayer for healing can go alongside medical care, and an individual testimony does not in itself establish either the cause of improvement or a miraculous healing.
concerns_en: Jesus's casting out of the unclean spirit in Mark 9 provides no basis for interpreting narcolepsy or cataplexy as demonic activity or for recommending that passage as therapy for these illnesses. In the attached translation, verse 29 states that such a spirit can come out only by prayer; the podcast's citation adds fasting, which does not match that translation.

If testimony about the disappearance of symptoms is conveyed as confirmation of miraculous healing or as a promise to others, that would require cautious verification and must not replace medical evaluation or treatment. The Church encourages prayer for health, but at the same time emphasizes that it does not dispense with daily care and medical treatment of the sick.

The expression that one should never rely on man can be overly broad: Christian trust in God does not exclude reasonable trust, cooperation, and seeking help from other human beings. Jesus and Mary are also not on the same level: Mary is a creature and intercessor, while Christ is the only Savior.

sections.subtitle_en: Ivanka's testimony: narcolepsy, fasting, and the message not to trust in man
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host reads Ivanka's testimony about the disappearance of symptoms of narcolepsy and cataplexy
sections.content_en:
In the part dedicated to healings, Grebenar reads the testimony of viewer **Ivanka**. She writes that through fasting and prayer with Ora et Labora she has no symptoms of **narcolepsy and cataplexy**.

Ivanka states that in agreement with a female neurologist from Zagreb she stopped taking medications a long time ago. Nevertheless, she could still feel fatigue after meals and mild symptoms of cataplexy. She has suffered from the illness since the seventh grade of elementary school, and now she is 33 years old. To those suffering from narcolepsy and cataplexy, she recommends reading the passage about the epileptic boy from the **Gospel of Mark, chapter 9, verses 14 to 29**, with Jesus' words: "This kind cannot be driven out by anything but prayer and fasting."

She adds that during fasting she can function normally, but always in prayer listens carefully whether she is called to a particular fast or not. The testimony concludes with the sentence: "I do not honor and glorify Vladimir, but Jesus Christ, the Father, and the Holy Spirit." She considers Vladimir, she writes, an ordinary man who wants by his life to do the will of the Father and who often encourages the faithful to prayer, helping others, and obedience to the Church.

Grebenar is delighted. "Bravo. How beautifully you wrote this," he says, praising especially the concluding part. On that he builds the message: **one should never trust in man**. Man can fail and disappoint, but Jesus never. He openly admits that he himself can also disappoint people. As an example, he mentions Judas, who was with Jesus for three and a half years, and then betrayed him.

The conclusion is in line with the episode's title. People can disappoint one another, but Jesus and the Blessed Virgin Mary never. That is why **Jesus must be in first place, and then everything will fall into its proper place**.

sections.subtitle: Krunica diljem Hrvatske i centar Kraljica Mira u Međugorju
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar opisuje svoj privatni projekt Međunarodnog edukacijskog centra Kraljica Mira u Međugorju
sections.content:
Pred kraj emisije Grebenar poziva na **molitvu krunice u svim hrvatskim gradovima** u subotu, za dva do tri dana. Najavljuje i da Hrvati iz dijaspore organiziraju prijevoz iz **Njemačke i Austrije** na molitvu krunice na glavnom trgu u **Zagrebu**. Kontakti su prikazani na ekranu, a voditelj ističe da se još stigne prijaviti i spremiti za put. Zatim udjeljuje blagoslov: „Neka se sveta Mati sa svojim Sinom i svetim Josipom udostoji blagoslov nam dati, u ime Oca i Sina i Duha Svetoga.“

Na kraju govori o svom **privatnom projektu Međunarodnog edukacijskog centra Kraljica Mira**. Bit će to, kaže, svojevrsni centar za navjestitelje Božje riječi iz različitih područja, primjerice poduzetništva i medicine. Projekt je pokrenuo vlastitim sredstvima, ponajviše prihodima od knjiga i novcem koji je uštedio. Sada ga mora dovršiti.

Opisuje i lokaciju u **Međugorju**. Prostor se nalazi tri do četiri stotine metara iza pošte, od kružnog toka u smjeru Čitluka, s lijeve strane, gdje su dvije zgrade. Projekt je u prizemlju jedne od njih, ima preko 300 kvadratnih metara i praktički je pred uporabnom dozvolom.

Grebenar naglašava da od projekta ne očekuje nikakvu financijsku korist, iako je riječ o velikom trošku. Sve je kalkulacije, kaže, predao Gospodinu i ne želi o tome razmišljati. Odbacuje i optužbe kojima je bio izložen: „Nisam gradio sebi nikakve vile i rezidencije, kako su me napadali, već naprotiv centar gdje će se navještati riječ Božja.“

Potrebna su mu još dodatna financijska sredstva. Dio će, kaže, sigurno dati iz vlastite imovine, a sve koji osjete poticaj poziva da pomognu **kupnjom knjiga**. Zahvaljuje svima koji već pomažu na taj način i blagoslivlja ih.

Emisiju zatvara pozivom: „Prati svaki dan Ora et Labora. Neka je sve na veću slavu Božju.“

magisterium.assessment: Poziv na krunicu, navještaj Božje riječi i osnivanje edukacijskog centra za evangelizaciju u načelu su usklađeni s katoličkim poslanjem, a molitva se može razumjeti kao zaziv Božje pomoći po zagovoru Marije i svetoga Josipa. Ipak, formulacija da se Marija i Josip „udostoje blagoslov nam dati” može biti jasnija kako ne bi ostavila dojam da blagoslov potječe od njih neovisno o Bogu; iz sažetka se ne mogu procijeniti financijska transparentnost ni crkveni nadzor projekta.
concerns: Izraz o Mariji i svetom Josipu koji daju blagoslov teološki je dvoznačan; preciznije bi bilo izričito moliti Boga za blagoslov po njihovu zagovoru.

Poziv na kupnju knjiga radi dovršetka privatnog projekta sam po sebi nije protivan katoličkom nauku, ali dostupni opis ne omogućuje procjenu transparentnosti financiranja niti odnosa centra prema nadležnoj crkvenoj vlasti.
magisterium.enrichment: Krunica je katolička molitva usmjerena na razmatranje Kristova otajstva, a crkveni nauk potiče njezinu osobnu i zajedničku molitvu kao potporu evangelizaciji i miru. Evangelizacija treba imati Krista u središtu te uključuje i navještaj i svjedočenje života; zato je zamisao o osposobljavanju navjestitelja načelno prikladna, ako program ostane vjeran Evanđelju i crkvenom poslanju.
magisterium.assessment_en: The call to the rosary, proclamation of the Word of God, and the establishment of an education center for evangelization are in principle aligned with the Catholic mission, and the prayer can be understood as an invocation of God's help through the intercession of Mary and Saint Joseph. Nevertheless, the phrasing that Mary and Joseph “deign to give us a blessing” could be clearer so as not to leave the impression that the blessing originates from them independently of God; from the summary, financial transparency and church oversight of the project cannot be evaluated.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Rosary is a Catholic prayer focused on contemplating the mystery of Christ, and church teaching encourages its personal and communal recitation as support for evangelization and peace. Evangelization must have Christ at its center and includes both proclamation and the witness of life; therefore, the idea of training proclaimers is in principle appropriate, if the program remains faithful to the Gospel and the Church's mission.
concerns_en: The phrasing about Mary and Saint Joseph giving a blessing is theologically ambiguous; it would be more precise to explicitly pray to God for a blessing through their intercession.

The call to purchase books in order to complete a private project is not in itself contrary to Catholic teaching, but the available description does not allow for an assessment of the transparency of funding or the center's relationship to competent church authority.

sections.subtitle_en: Rosary throughout Croatia and the Queen of Peace center in Međugorje
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar describes his private project of the Queen of Peace International Educational Center in Međugorje
sections.content_en:
Toward the end of the show, Grebenar calls for the **prayer of the Rosary in all Croatian cities** on Saturday, in two to three days. He also announces that Croats from the diaspora are organizing transportation from **Germany and Austria** for the prayer of the Rosary in the main square in **Zagreb**. Contacts are shown on the screen, and the host emphasizes that there is still time to sign up and get ready for the trip. Then he imparts a blessing: "May the holy Mother with her Son and Saint Joseph deign to give us a blessing, in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit."

At the end, he speaks about his **private project of the Queen of Peace International Educational Center**. It will be, he says, a kind of center for proclaimers of God's word from various fields, such as entrepreneurship and medicine. He launched the project with his own funds, mostly proceeds from books and money he had saved. Now he must complete it.

He also describes the location in **Međugorje**. The premises are located three to four hundred meters behind the post office, from the roundabout in the direction of Čitluk, on the left side, where there are two buildings. The project is on the ground floor of one of them, has over 300 square meters, and is practically before obtaining an occupancy permit.

Grebenar emphasizes that he expects no financial benefit from the project, even though it represents a great expense. All calculations, he says, he has surrendered to the Lord and does not want to think about it. He also rejects the accusations to which he was subjected: "I did not build myself any villas and residences, as they attacked me, but on the contrary a center where the word of God will be proclaimed."

He still needs additional financial resources. Part, he says, he will certainly give from his own assets, and all who feel prompted he invites to help by **purchasing books**. He thanks everyone who is already helping in this way and blesses them.

He closes the show with an invitation: "Follow Ora et Labora every day. May everything be to the greater glory of God."

iterations.theme_en: Interpretation of the Epistle to the Philippians and the gospel of the lost sheep (Jesus in first place, joy over the conversion of a sinner) and announcements of the patriotic initiative Ora et Labora
